questions.e: Standard procedure for sudden deaths; the cause was cardiac arrest.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Eleven crew were injured when their vessel was hit by a projectile. The immediate danger in such blast injuries is:

B. Is too large to inhale

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An oil spill from a damaged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz would most directly threaten:

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.e: Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel were honoured on 5 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: Zoology

o: A. Lack A and B antigens
B. Carry both A and B antigens

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Zoology

o: A. Internet-based video and data communication
questions.e: 50 crore consultations show digital health at population scale.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for:
o: A. The IceCube Neutrino Observatory and high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
questions.e: Francis Halzen; announced 6 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Neutrinos are best described as:
o: A. Nearly massless particles that barely interact with matter
questions.e: Which is why IceCube needs a cubic kilometre of ice to catch a few.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: IceCube is located at the:
questions.e: Thousands of optical sensors frozen into Antarctic ice.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: World Cerebral Palsy Day 2026 was observed on:
questions.e: Raising awareness on inclusion, accessibility and equal participation.

questions.q: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as captain of:

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: The 72nd National Wildlife Week (2026) theme is:
questions.e: Observed 2–8 October 2026.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Delhi's AQI touched 238 (poor) at Alipur on 6 Oct. PM2.5 is most harmful because it:
o: A. Penetrates deep into the lungs and bloodstream
questions.e: Fine particles ≤2.5 µm cross the alveolar barrier; poor AQI aggravates asthma and COPD.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Very light rain or drizzle over Delhi can lower AQI mainly by:
o: A. Washing suspended particulates out of the air
questions.e: Wet deposition scavenges PM10/PM2.5; that is why post-rain air usually reads cleaner.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Pneumonic plague, suspected in cases being monitored in Russia, is caused by:
questions.e: A bacterial infection of the lungs; as reported on 6 Oct, India's IMA says there is no immediate threat to India.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The WHO says global life expectancy has nearly returned to its pre-pandemic level. Life expectancy at birth is:
o: A. The average years a newborn is expected to live
C. The median age of a population
questions.e: It is a summary mortality measure, sensitive to pandemic-era excess deaths.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: India's 4-gold, 1-silver IOAA haul celebrates astronomy. The human eye's light-sensitive cells are the:
o: A. Rods and cones of the retina
questions.e: Rods handle low light; cones handle colour — the biology behind stargazing.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Heroin, the drug in Delhi Police's 6 Oct bust, is derived from:
questions.e: Heroin is a semi-synthetic opioid made from morphine extracted from poppy latex.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Drizzle forms when cloud droplets coalesce and fall. The process is part of the:
questions.e: Condensation → coalescence → precipitation; IMD forecast very light rain for Delhi today.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A by-election and a general election differ in that a by-election:
o: A. Fills a seat that fell vacant mid-term
C. Is held every five years
questions.e: Six by-elections vote today after April-2026 winners resigned one of two seats.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Channelrhodopsin, central to optogenetics, was discovered in:
questions.e: Hegemann and Nagel found the light-sensitive protein in this single-celled alga.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In optogenetics, illuminating channelrhodopsin with blue light causes:
o: A. An ion channel to open, letting ions flow
B. The cell wall to thicken
questions.e: Light opens the channel; ions flow through the protein — a switch neuroscientists had long dreamed of.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Deisseroth's 2005 breakthrough demonstrated optogenetics in:
questions.e: He genetically engineered rat nerve cells to produce channelrhodopsin, then triggered nerve signals with light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ion channels like channelrhodopsin are embedded in the:
questions.e: Membrane proteins that gate ion flow — the basis of nerve impulses.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Optogenetics is now used to study neural circuits behind:
questions.e: It reveals circuits relevant to neurological and psychiatric disorders, and is being explored to restore sight.

questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which pair discovered channelrhodopsin?
questions.e: Hegemann (Max Planck, then Humboldt Berlin) and Nagel (Würzburg); Deisseroth turned it into a neural switch.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Floods like the Gandak's raise the risk of which water-borne disease?
questions.e: Vibrio cholerae spreads through contaminated water; floods contaminate drinking-water sources.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Stagnant floodwater is a breeding ground for:
questions.e: Anopheles breeds in stagnant water, so malaria risk spikes after floods.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A deficient monsoon (87% of the long-period average) most directly stresses:
o: A. Kharif crops at sowing and vegetative stages
questions.e: Kharif crops depend on the southwest monsoon for sowing and early growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Waterlogging after floods damages crop roots mainly by:
o: A. Cutting off oxygen (anoxia) to roots
questions.e: Root respiration needs oxygen; waterlogged soils turn anaerobic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Paper archives like the 8.5-lakh-book Central Secretariat Library decay mainly because of:
o: A. Fungi and insects thriving in damp storage
questions.e: Paper biodeterioration: fungi and silverfish attack cellulose in humid conditions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Idling vehicles at congested signals emit high levels of:
questions.e: Incomplete combustion at idle raises carbon monoxide and hydrocarbon emissions — a respiratory-health hazard.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The structural and functional unit of the human kidney is the:
questions.e: About a million nephrons per kidney filter blood and form urine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a normal human somatic cell, the number of autosomes is:
questions.e: 46 chromosomes = 44 autosomes + 2 sex chromosomes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Leprosy is caused by:
questions.e: Hansen's disease; 3,832 child cases reported in India, which targets transmission interruption by 2027.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Multidrug therapy for leprosy includes:
questions.e: MDT cures leprosy; early treatment prevents disability.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mycobacterium leprae is best described as:
questions.e: Discovered by Hansen in 1873; it is an obligate intracellular acid-fast bacterium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: El Niño is associated with:
o: A. Weakening of the Walker circulation and deficient monsoons
questions.e: The 2026 monsoon ended at 87% of LPA under a strong El Niño.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A monsoon at 87% of the long-period average is classified as:
questions.e: 759.4 mm for 2026; 17 of 36 subdivisions were deficient.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nepal's plan to drain glacial lakes addresses:
questions.e: GLOFs are a growing Himalayan climate risk after deadly floods.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: India's leprosy elimination drive is run under:
o: A. The National Leprosy Eradication Programme
B. The National Vector Borne Disease Programme
questions.e: NLEP targets interruption of transmission by 2027.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Hockey drag-flicks demand explosive leg power, supplied mainly by:
questions.e: Type II fibres contract rapidly for sprint and strike power — Harmanpreet's 12th-minute drag-flick in the 5-1 final.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Neeru Dhanda's record 28/28 trap final rests on precise eye–hand coordination, integrated in the:
questions.e: The cerebellum fine-tunes motor coordination and balance — key to hitting 28 straight clays.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: After a bout, wrestlers' burning muscles clear which accumulated metabolite?
questions.e: Anaerobic glycolysis in intense effort (Antim Panghal's 53kg final) produces lactate; oxygen debt is repaid in recovery.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Post-match, the parasympathetic system slows the athlete's heart via:
questions.e: Vagal acetylcholine release counters the sympathetic surge once the final whistle blows.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Rubidium atomic clocks aboard NVS-03 keep time using:
o: A. Hyperfine transitions of rubidium atoms
questions.e: Atomic clocks count the ultra-stable microwave hyperfine transition — NVS-03 launches 15–20 Oct to restore NavIC.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Rickets in growing athletes is prevented by adequate:
questions.e: Vitamin D enables calcium absorption for bone mineralisation; deficiency softens growing bones.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A GNSS receiver needs 4 satellite signals because it solves:
o: A. 3 position coordinates + its own clock drift
questions.e: Four unknowns need four independent voices — with 3 working NavIC satellites, standalone 3-D fixes are impossible.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Athletes beating jet lag to Nagoya rely on the circadian hormone:
questions.e: Pineal melatonin entrains the sleep–wake cycle to the new light–dark schedule.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A captain who fights off an attacker mid-flight is flooded with which 'fight-or-flight' hormone?
questions.e: Adrenaline (epinephrine) from the adrenal medulla drives the acute stress response — heart rate, alertness, energy mobilisation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Hingoli earthquake's magnitude was measured on a scale that is:
questions.e: The Richter scale is logarithmic: each whole-number step is ~10× the wave amplitude and ~31.6× the seismic energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Earthquake waves are first recorded by a:
questions.e: A seismograph records ground motion; the 4.5-magnitude Hingoli tremor was reported by the National Center for Seismology.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which vitamin is central to the astronaut nutrition plans under ISRO's Santulan-style programmes?
questions.e: Balanced crew nutrition covers all micronutrients — A for vision, B12 for red cells, K for clotting, D for bone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The diaphragm is the chief muscle of:
questions.e: Diaphragmatic contraction expands the thoracic cavity, driving inhalation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Xylem in plants chiefly transports:
questions.e: Xylem carries water/minerals upward; phloem translocates photosynthates.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The normal pH of human blood is:
questions.e: Blood pH is tightly buffered at ~7.35–7.45 by the bicarbonate system.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A hockey goalkeeper's explosive penalty-stroke save is powered first by ATP regenerated via:
questions.e: Instant, oxygen-independent ATP for ~10 seconds of maximal effort — Savita Punia's save vs Zhang Ying, 2 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An archer sighting a target 70 m away relies on the eye's:
questions.e: Ciliary muscles adjust lens curvature to focus distant targets — the skill behind India's 5–3 archery gold.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Wrestlers cutting weight rapidly risk dangerous:
questions.e: Rapid dehydration depletes Na⁺/K⁺ — a sports-medicine staple.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Insulin is secreted by the:
o: A. Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans
B. Alpha cells of the islets
questions.e: Beta cells release insulin in response to high blood glucose; alpha cells release glucagon.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The universal RBC recipient blood group is:
questions.e: AB⁺ red cells carry A, B and Rh antigens, so no anti-A/anti-B antibodies — can receive from all groups.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Upward transport of water and minerals in plants occurs through the:
questions.e: Xylem vessels carry the transpiration stream; phloem translocates food.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mendel's monohybrid F2 phenotypic ratio is:
questions.e: 3 dominant : 1 recessive; the genotypic ratio is 1:2:1.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During inhalation, the diaphragm:
questions.e: Contraction increases thoracic volume, dropping pressure below atmospheric — air flows in.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: ISRO's 'Santulan' programme relates to:
o: A. Nutrition planning for Gaganyaan astronauts
questions.e: Santulan hires four nutritionists at Bengaluru's Human Space Flight Centre for custom astronaut meal plans.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: Each nephron filters blood at the glomerulus and fine-tunes urine through tubular reabsorption/secretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Universal blood donor group is:
questions.e: O− red cells lack A, B and Rh antigens, so they can be transfused to any ABO/Rh recipient in emergencies.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Photosynthesis occurs in the:
questions.e: Chlorophyll in thylakoid membranes captures light; the Calvin cycle fixes CO₂ in the stroma.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of vitamin:
questions.e: Vitamin A forms retinal in rhodopsin; deficiency impairs dim-light vision — a classic nutrition-fact link to Santulan.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In DNA, adenine pairs with:
questions.e: A–T (2 H-bonds) and G–C (3 H-bonds) — Chargaff's rule; uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: The 157th Gandhi Jayanti in 2026 marks the birth year:
questions.e: 2026 − 157 = 1869; Gandhi was born 2 October 1869 — also the UN International Day of Non-Violence.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Rubidium atomic clocks on NVS-03 exploit which atomic property?
questions.e: Atomic clocks count the ultra-stable hyperfine transition of Rb atoms — the timekeeping heart of NavIC.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 16. In angiosperms, triple fusion produces the:
questions.e: One male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei/secondary nucleus, usually forming a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 17. Crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs during which meiotic substage?
questions.e: Synapsis begins in zygotene; exchange between non-sister chromatids occurs in pachytene. Chiasmata become visible later in diplotene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 18. Most carbon dioxide in human blood is transported as:
questions.e: Carbonic anhydrase in red cells speeds conversion to bicarbonate, which carries the largest fraction of CO₂ in blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 19. Which nephron segment is highly permeable to water but comparatively less permeable to electrolytes?
questions.e: The descending limb allows water to leave into the hyperosmotic medulla; the ascending limb is nearly impermeable to water and transports salts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 20. Apical dominance is chiefly associated with:
o: A. Auxin from the shoot apex
questions.e: Auxin produced near the shoot apex suppresses lateral bud growth; removing the apex commonly releases axillary buds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 21. Antibodies are secreted mainly by:
questions.e: Antigen-stimulated B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that secrete immunoglobulins and memory B cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 22. Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
questions.e: Energy is lost as heat at each transfer, so available energy necessarily decreases from lower to higher trophic levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 23. During PCR, primers attach to complementary template sequences in the:
questions.e: Heat separates strands during denaturation; cooling permits primer annealing; thermostable polymerase extends from those primers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 24. Restriction endonucleases are valuable in cloning because they:
o: B. Cut DNA at specific recognition sites
questions.e: They recognise characteristic sequences and cleave DNA; DNA ligase, not the restriction enzyme, joins compatible fragments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 25. A test cross of a heterozygous monohybrid Aa produces which genotypic ratio?
questions.e: Aa × aa yields half Aa and half aa. The 1:1 result reveals that the tested dominant parent was heterozygous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 26. The AB blood group demonstrates:
questions.e: IA and IB are both expressed in an IAIB individual; neither masks the other. Both are dominant over i.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 27. Stomatal opening in many plants is promoted by:
o: B. Guard-cell K⁺ uptake and water entry
questions.e: Ion accumulation lowers guard-cell water potential, water enters osmotically, turgor increases and the pore opens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 28. The acrosome of a sperm is derived from the:
questions.e: During spermiogenesis, the Golgi forms the acrosomal cap containing enzymes that assist penetration of egg coverings.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 29. Insulin is secreted by which pancreatic cell type?
questions.e: Beta cells of the islets secrete insulin; alpha cells secrete glucagon. Insulin generally lowers blood glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 30. Primary succession differs from secondary succession because it begins:
o: C. On a substrate lacking a previous community and developed soil
questions.e: Primary succession begins on a lifeless surface such as bare rock; secondary succession begins where a community existed earlier.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 31. For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 3 mol H₂ mixed with 2 mol O₂ gives a maximum of:
questions.e: Three moles of H₂ need 1.5 mol O₂, so H₂ is limiting and produces 3 mol H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 32. How many orbitals are present in the n = 3 shell?
questions.e: The number of orbitals in shell n is n², so 3² = 9. The maximum electron capacity is 2n² = 18.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 33. The H–N–H bond angle in NH₃ is smaller than the tetrahedral angle mainly because:
o: A. Nitrogen has no lone pair
B. Lone pair–bond pair repulsion is stronger
questions.e: One lone pair occupies more space than a bonding pair and compresses the three N–H bonds to about 107°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 34. Raising temperature shifts an exothermic equilibrium:
o: D. Only if a catalyst is present
questions.e: Heat behaves like a product for an exothermic reaction, so adding heat favours the reverse direction and decreases the forward equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 35. The pH of 1.0 × 10⁻³ M HCl, treated as fully dissociated, is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 36. At fixed temperature, osmotic pressure of an ideal dilute non-electrolyte solution is:
questions.e: The van ’t Hoff equation is π = CRT; for association or dissociation it becomes π = iCRT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 37. If E°cathode = +0.34 V and E°anode = −0.76 V, E°cell is:
questions.e: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 38. The unit of the rate constant for a second-order reaction is:
questions.e: Rate has concentration/time units. For rate = k[A]², k has concentration⁻¹ time⁻¹ = L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 39. Lanthanoid contraction is mainly caused by poor shielding by:
questions.e: The 4f electrons shield nuclear charge poorly, producing a progressive size decrease across the lanthanoids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 40. In [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃, cobalt oxidation state and coordination number are:
questions.e: NH₃ is neutral and three external Cl⁻ require a 3+ complex. Six monodentate NH₃ ligands give coordination number 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 41. Anti-Markovnikov addition in the peroxide effect is characteristically observed with:
questions.e: The radical chain energetics make the peroxide effect useful for HBr; it is not generally observed for HCl or HI.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 42. Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because:
o: A. Phenol has more hydrogen atoms
questions.e: Negative charge in phenoxide delocalises over the aromatic ring, whereas ethoxide lacks comparable resonance stabilisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 43. A positive Tollens’ test is commonly shown by:
questions.e: Aldehydes reduce the diamminesilver(I) reagent to metallic silver while being oxidised; ordinary ketones generally do not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 44. Which carbohydrate is non-reducing?
questions.e: In sucrose, both anomeric carbons participate in the glycosidic bond, leaving no free hemiacetal/hemiketal group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 45. In Lassaigne’s test, covalent nitrogen is converted into:
questions.e: Fusion with sodium converts carbon and nitrogen in the compound into ionic NaCN, which is then detected through subsequent reactions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 46. Which is the dimensional formula of pressure?
questions.e: Pressure = force/area, so dimensions are (MLT⁻²)/L² = ML⁻¹T⁻².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 47. The area under a velocity–time graph between two instants gives:
questions.e: Integrating velocity over time gives displacement. The slope of the same graph gives acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 48. A block rests on a rough horizontal surface with no horizontal applied force. The static friction is:
questions.e: Static friction adjusts to oppose a tendency of relative motion; with no horizontal tendency it is zero, not automatically μsN.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 49. The net work done on a body equals its change in:
questions.e: The work–energy theorem states Wnet = ΔK, regardless of whether individual forces are conservative.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 50. If external torque on a system is zero, which quantity is conserved?
questions.e: Zero external torque implies dL/dt = 0. Angular speed may still change if the moment of inertia changes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 51. Compared with a satellite in a higher circular orbit, one in a lower circular orbit has:
questions.e: v = √(GM/r), so decreasing orbital radius increases speed. The lower orbit also has a shorter period.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 52. In steady horizontal ideal-fluid flow through a narrower pipe section, speed and pressure respectively:
questions.e: Continuity makes speed rise where area falls; Bernoulli then requires lower static pressure at the faster section.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 53. If absolute temperature becomes four times, rms molecular speed becomes:
questions.e: vrms ∝ √T, so multiplying temperature by 4 multiplies rms speed by 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 54. At the mean position of ideal SHM, the particle has:
o: A. Maximum speed and zero acceleration
B. Zero speed and maximum acceleration
C. Zero speed and zero acceleration
questions.e: At x = 0, a = −ω²x = 0 and energy is entirely kinetic, so speed is maximum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 55. The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is:
questions.e: Wave speed rises with tension T and falls with linear mass density μ: v = √(T/μ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 56. The electric field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is:
questions.e: Free charges rearrange until the internal electric field vanishes; the conductor is then an equipotential.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 57. A dielectric of constant K fully fills an isolated parallel-plate capacitor. Its capacitance becomes:
questions.e: With geometry fixed, C = εA/d, and ε becomes Kε₀, so capacitance is multiplied by K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 58. A charged particle moving exactly parallel to a uniform magnetic field experiences magnetic force:
questions.e: F = qvB sinθ and θ = 0°, so the magnetic force is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 59. Lenz’s law states that induced current produces a field that:
o: A. Supports the change in flux
B. Opposes the change in flux
D. Has no relation to flux
questions.e: The induced effect opposes the change that produced it, consistent with conservation of energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 60. Forward bias of a p–n junction:
questions.e: Forward bias reduces the potential barrier and depletion width, allowing majority carriers to cross readily.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 61. A satellite of mass m orbits Earth at height h above the surface (Earth radius R, mass M). The gravitational force on it equals:
questions.e: Inverse-square law with the centre-to-centre distance r = R + h, so F = GmM/r² = GmM/(R + h)².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 62. A 4 μF capacitor charged to 100 V stores energy equal to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 63. In a p–n junction diode under reverse bias, the depletion region:
o: A. Widens and the current stays near zero
C. Conducts heavily in both directions
D. Converts to an n-type layer
questions.e: Reverse bias pulls majority carriers away from the junction, widening the depletion layer; only a tiny drift current of minority carriers flows.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 64. The oxidation state of cobalt in [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ is:
questions.e: NH₃ is neutral and each Cl is −1: x + 0 + 3(−1) = 0 gives x = +3.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 65. Denosumab — the reference product of the biosimilar DEGEVMA approved by the US FDA in Sep 2026 — acts by:
o: A. Inhibiting RANKL, blocking osteoclast formation and bone resorption
B. Binding oestrogen receptors in bone
C. Chelating calcium in blood plasma
questions.e: Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody against RANKL (receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand); blocking RANKL stops osteoclasts from resorbing bone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 66. Naloxone, for which WHO invited prequalification submissions in Sep 2026, is used in:
o: A. Emergency reversal of opioid overdose
questions.e: Naloxone is an opioid-receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses respiratory depression in opioid overdose; WHO invited manufacturers to submit it (with methadone and buprenorphine) for prequalification.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 67. Atebrioz (zilurgisertib), approved by the US FDA on 25 Sep 2026 as a once-daily oral ALK2 inhibitor, is indicated to:
o: A. Reduce new heterotopic ossification in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
B. Lower LDL cholesterol in familial hypercholesterolaemia
C. Treat extensive-stage small cell lung cancer
questions.e: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva is a rare disorder in which soft tissues progressively turn to bone; in the Phase 2 PROGRESS trial, new bone growth fell by 3.2 cm³ on zilurgisertib while it rose 24.6 cm³ on placebo.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 68. A biosimilar medicine (e.g. DEGEVMA, FDA-approved in Sep 2026) is defined as:
o: A. A biologic highly similar to an approved reference product with no clinically meaningful differences
B. An exact chemical copy of the reference drug
C. A weaker, over-the-counter version of the reference drug
D. A drug with a completely different active ingredient
questions.e: Unlike small-molecule generics, biosimilars are large complex proteins; regulators require proof of high similarity and no clinically meaningful differences from the reference biologic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 69. Which phase of the cell cycle is the longest in a typical eukaryotic cell?
questions.e: G1 phase is the longest phase in most eukaryotic cells, during which the cell grows and carries out normal functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 70. The phenotypic ratio of a dihybrid cross (F2 generation) is:
questions.e: A dihybrid cross gives the classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 71. The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: The nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 72. The site of photosynthesis in a plant cell is the:
questions.e: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplast, which contains chlorophyll.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 73. The pyramid of energy in any ecosystem is always:
questions.e: The pyramid of energy is always upright because energy is lost at each trophic level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 74. Crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs during which sub-stage of prophase I?
questions.e: Crossing over occurs during pachytene, when homologous chromosomes are fully synapsed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 75. A person with blood group O is called a universal donor because:
o: A. Their plasma has no antibodies
B. Their RBCs have no A or B antigens
C. Their blood has no Rh factor
D. Their WBCs accept all antigens
questions.e: Group O RBCs lack A and B antigens, so they are not attacked by anti-A or anti-B antibodies in the recipient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 76. The bond formed between two amino acid molecules during protein synthesis is called a:
questions.e: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another, releasing water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 77. The nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in the root nodules of leguminous plants is:
questions.e: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in legume root nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 78. Besides the nucleus, which organelle contains its own circular DNA in animal cells?
questions.e: Mitochondria contain their own circular DNA and ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
