questions.q: 81. A body of mass 2 kg moving at 3 m/s has kinetic energy:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 82. The powerhouse of the cell is the:
questions.e: Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 83. The universal donor blood group is:
questions.e: O negative red cells lack A, B and Rh antigens, so they can be given to any recipient.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 84. Avogadro's number is approximately:
questions.e: One mole contains 6.022 × 10²³ entities.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 85. The SI unit of force is the:
questions.e: Force = mass × acceleration, measured in newtons (kg·m/s²).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 86. Photosynthesis occurs mainly in the:
questions.e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, the pigment that captures light energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 87. The atomic number of carbon is:
questions.e: Carbon has 6 protons, hence atomic number 6 (mass number 12).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 88. The approximate value of acceleration due to gravity on Earth is:
questions.e: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² near Earth's surface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: 89. The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: Each nephron filters blood and forms urine; a kidney has about a million nephrons.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for:
o: Non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis
questions.e: Awarded to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai; announced 7 Oct 2026 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

questions.q: Autocatalysis, recognised in the 2026 Chemistry Nobel, is a reaction in which:
o: A product of the reaction acts as its own catalyst
An external enzyme speeds it up
questions.e: Central to Kagan and Soai's work on asymmetric synthesis.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature went to:
questions.e: Announced 8 Oct 2026 by the Swedish Academy.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was announced on:
questions.e: Winners: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford.

questions.q: India beat the West Indies by 14 runs in the T20I played on 11 Oct 2026 at:
questions.e: India 223/10 beat West Indies 209/7; Abhishek Sharma 69 off 30.

questions.q: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit will take charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on:
questions.e: He succeeds Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was announced on:
questions.e: Awarded to Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel for optogenetics by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet.

questions.q: Optogenetics, recognised by the 2026 Medicine Nobel, involves:
questions.e: Light-gated ion channels switch nerve cells on/off with light.

questions.q: TRISHNA, the Indo-French satellite in an advanced stage, will study:
o: Water resources via thermal infra-red imaging
questions.e: For better management of water resources; open-data policy.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to:
questions.e: Announced 8 Oct 2026.

questions.q: NVS-03, set for launch on 15–20 Oct 2026, belongs to which system:
questions.e: NavIC (earlier IRNSS) — India's regional navigation system; NVS-03 would restore the four-satellite minimum.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for:
o: Discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics
questions.e: Karl Deisseroth (US, Stanford), Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel (Germany) — announced 5 Oct 2026 by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet.

questions.q: Channelrhodopsin, the protein behind optogenetics, was discovered in:
questions.e: Hegemann and Nagel found channelrhodopsin in Chlamydomonas; Deisseroth turned it into a light-controlled switch for nerve cells (2026 Medicine Nobel).

questions.q: India's reported quantum-secure communication network has now reached:
questions.e: Reported 11 Oct 2026: the quantum-secure communication network has reached 1,000 km against a 2,000-km target.

questions.q: The foundation stone of ICMR's High Altitude Medical and Public Health Research Centre will be laid at Kelong on:
questions.e: The Union Health Minister lays the foundation stone at Kelong on 12 Oct 2026 (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

questions.q: From 15 October 2026, the new UPI Merchant Discount Rate is:
o: 0.4% on specified merchant payments above ₹2,000 (capped at ₹300)
A flat ₹5 on every UPI transaction
questions.e: P2P transfers remain free; merchant payments up to ₹2,000 stay outside the framework.

questions.q: 'Mangrole', the vessel the Indian Navy is set to induct, is:
questions.e: The Navy announced the induction of indigenous anti-submarine warfare vessel Mangrole (PIB, 10 Oct 2026).

questions.q: Exercise Konkan-2026, for which INS Trishul reached Plymouth, is India's bilateral naval exercise with:
questions.e: Konkan is the Indo-UK bilateral naval exercise (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

questions.q: INS Sahyadri reached Vladivostok for Exercise Indra-2026 with:
questions.e: Indra is the India–Russia bilateral exercise (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Photorespiration is initiated in the:
questions.e: Photorespiration begins in the chloroplast when RuBisCO oxygenates RuBP; the pathway then cycles through the peroxisome and mitochondria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The ABO blood group antigens are chemically:
o: Glycoproteins and glycolipids on the RBC surface
questions.e: ABO antigens are oligosaccharide chains attached to proteins and lipids on the red cell membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which hormone secreted by the placenta maintains the corpus luteum in early pregnancy?
questions.e: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) maintains the corpus luteum until the placenta takes over progesterone production.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of inductance is:
questions.e: Inductance is measured in henry (H); 1 H = 1 Wb/A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH3–CH=CH–CHO is:
questions.e: The aldehyde carbon gets priority as C1, placing the double bond at C2: but-2-enal (common name crotonaldehyde).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A Barr body is:
o: An inactivated X chromosome in female somatic cells
questions.e: The Barr body is the condensed, transcriptionally inactive X chromosome in mammalian female somatic cells (Lyon hypothesis).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula of the universal gravitational constant G is:
questions.e: From F = Gm₁m₂/r², [G] = [Fr²/m²] = MLT⁻²·L²/M² = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following pairs has the same dimensions?
questions.e: Work = force × displacement and torque = r × F both have dimensions [ML²T⁻²]; the other pairs differ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The number of significant figures in 0.004080 is:
questions.e: Leading zeros are not significant; the digits 4, 0, 8, 0 are all significant, giving four significant figures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One parsec is approximately equal to:
questions.e: 1 parsec ≈ 3.26 light years ≈ 3.08 × 10¹⁶ m, the distance at which 1 AU subtends one arcsecond.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the relation y = a sin(ωt − kx), the dimensions of k are:
questions.e: The argument of a trigonometric function is dimensionless, so kx is dimensionless and [k] = 1/[x] = [L⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of these is a dimensionless quantity?
questions.e: Refractive index is a ratio of speeds (c/v), hence dimensionless; the others carry dimensions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of the Stefan–Boltzmann constant σ is:
questions.e: From the Stefan–Boltzmann law E = σT⁴, [σ] = [E]/[T⁴] = W m⁻² K⁻⁴.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A physical quantity is measured as 4.25 ± 0.05. The percentage error is about:
questions.e: Percentage error = (0.05/4.25) × 100 ≈ 1.18%, about 1.2%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the error in measuring the radius of a sphere is 2%, the error in its volume is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which equation is dimensionally incorrect?
questions.e: vt² has dimensions LT², not length L; the other three are dimensionally consistent.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with velocity 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). The time to reach the highest point is:
questions.e: At the top v = 0, so t = u/g = 20/10 = 2 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a projectile given the same initial speed, the horizontal range is identical for angles:
questions.e: R = u²sin2θ/g is symmetric since sin2θ = sin2(90°−θ); e.g., 30° and 60° give the same range.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The maximum height H of a projectile projected at angle θ with speed u is:
questions.e: Using v_y² = u_y² − 2gH with v_y = 0 and u_y = u sinθ gives H = u²sin²θ/2g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the highest point of its trajectory, a projectile's acceleration is:
questions.e: Only gravity acts throughout the flight, so acceleration is g downward even though velocity is momentarily horizontal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car moves 30 km east and then 40 km north. The magnitude of its displacement is:
questions.e: Displacement = √(30² + 40²) = √2500 = 50 km, less than the 70 km path length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The slope of a velocity–time graph gives:
questions.e: Slope = dv/dt = acceleration; the area under the curve gives displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle in uniform circular motion of radius r with speed v has acceleration:
questions.e: Speed is constant but velocity direction changes continuously, giving centripetal acceleration v²/r toward the centre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train 200 m long crosses a 300 m bridge at 20 m/s. The crossing time is:
questions.e: Total distance = train length + bridge length = 500 m; t = 500/20 = 25 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: The area under a velocity–time graph gives displacement. Statement II: The slope of a displacement–time graph gives velocity.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: Area under v–t is ∫v dt = displacement, and slope of x–t is dx/dt = velocity; both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): A body can have zero velocity and non-zero acceleration. Reason (R): At the top of a vertical throw, velocity is zero but acceleration is g downward.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.e: At the highest point v = 0 momentarily while gravity still accelerates the body at g downward; R is a direct instance proving A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is dropped from a tower of height 45 m (g = 10 m/s²). The time to hit the ground is:
questions.e: h = ½gt² gives t = √(2h/g) = √(90/10) = 3 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two balls are thrown simultaneously from a tower, one upward and one downward, each at 20 m/s. They strike the ground with speeds that are:
questions.e: The upward-thrown ball returns to the throw level with 20 m/s downward, so both then fall identically and gain the same speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 5 kg mass experiences a net force of 20 N. Its acceleration is:
questions.e: From F = ma, a = 20/5 = 4 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The property of a body by which it resists any change in its state of rest or motion is called:
questions.e: Inertia, the essence of Newton's first law, is measured by the mass of the body.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gun of mass 4 kg fires a 20 g bullet at 300 m/s. The recoil speed of the gun is:
questions.e: Momentum conservation: 4V = 0.02 × 300 = 6, so V = 1.5 m/s opposite to the bullet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle of repose for a surface with coefficient of static friction μₛ = 1/√3 is:
questions.e: tanθ = μₛ = 1/√3 gives θ = 30°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block on a rough horizontal surface (μₖ = 0.3) slides with initial speed 6 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). The distance it travels before stopping is:
questions.e: Retardation a = μₖg = 3 m/s²; s = v²/2a = 36/6 = 6 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The banking angle θ for a curve of radius 100 m designed for a speed of 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²) satisfies:
questions.e: For banking without friction, tanθ = v²/rg = 400/1000 = 0.4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: Action and reaction forces act on different bodies. Statement II: Action and reaction can never cancel each other.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: Newton's third-law pairs always act on different bodies, so they cannot cancel; both statements are true.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): Static friction can do positive work on a body. Reason (R): Static friction opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Static friction accelerates a block placed on an accelerating truck, doing positive work on it; R is true but only describes friction's direction, not the sign of its work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 60 kg person stands in a lift accelerating upward at 2 m/s² (g = 10 m/s²). The apparent weight is:
questions.e: N − mg = ma gives N = m(g + a) = 60 × 12 = 720 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Impulse is equal to the:
questions.e: J = FΔt = Δp, the impulse–momentum theorem.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass m moving at speed v hits a wall and rebounds with the same speed. The impulse delivered to the wall is:
questions.e: Momentum change of the body is mv − (−mv) = 2mv, so the wall receives impulse 2mv.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a stone whirled in a vertical circle, the tension in the string is maximum at the:
questions.e: At the bottom T = mv²/r + mg, where tension must provide centripetal force and also support the weight.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 20 N pushes a box 10 m in the direction of the force. The work done is:
questions.e: W = Fs = 20 × 10 = 200 J since force and displacement are parallel.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work done in carrying a 10 kg suitcase horizontally over 5 m at constant speed is:
questions.e: The carrying force is vertical while displacement is horizontal (θ = 90°), so W = Fs cos90° = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the momentum of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.e: K = p²/2m, so doubling p multiplies K by four.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg body moving at 10 m/s has kinetic energy:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work–energy theorem states that the net work done on a body equals its:
questions.e: Wₙet = K_f − Kᵢ holds for any net force, conservative or not.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring of force constant 100 N/m is stretched by 0.2 m. The elastic potential energy stored is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two springs of force constants k₁ and k₂ joined in series have an equivalent constant of:
questions.e: For series combination 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂, giving k = k₁k₂/(k₁+k₂).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The power of an engine that does 6000 J of work in 2 minutes is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One horsepower is equal to:
questions.e: 1 hp = 746 W by definition, a unit of power.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass M and radius R about its central perpendicular axis is:
questions.e: All the mass of a thin ring lies at distance R from the axis, so I = MR².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a uniform disc of mass M and radius R about its central perpendicular axis is:
questions.e: For a disc the mass is spread from 0 to R, giving I = ½MR² about the central axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius of gyration K of a body is defined by the relation:
questions.e: K is the distance from the axis at which the whole mass M could be placed to give the same moment of inertia I = MK².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spinning figure skater pulls her arms inward. Her angular speed:
questions.e: Pulling in reduces I; with negligible external torque, L = Iω is conserved, so ω must rise.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Torque is the rotational analogue of:
questions.e: τ = r × F plays the role in rotation that force plays in translation (τ = Iα mirrors F = ma).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere rolls without slipping down an incline. At the contact point the condition satisfied is:
questions.e: No slipping means the contact point is instantaneously at rest: vᶜm − ωR = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angular momentum of a system is conserved when the:
questions.e: dL/dt = τₑxt, so L is constant exactly when the net external torque vanishes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The centre of mass of a uniform rod lies at its:
questions.e: Symmetry places the centre of mass of a uniform rod at its geometric centre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two masses m and 2m are separated by distance d. The centre of mass is at what distance from the mass m?
questions.e: xᶜm = (m·0 + 2m·d)/3m = 2d/3 from m, i.e., closer to the heavier mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): A hollow sphere has a larger moment of inertia than a solid sphere of the same mass and radius. Reason (R): In the hollow sphere the mass lies farther from the axis on average.
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: I = ⅔MR² (hollow) exceeds ⅖MR² (solid) precisely because its mass is concentrated at the rim, farther from the axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of torque is the:
questions.e: τ = rF has units of N·m (dimensionally same as joule, but reserved for torque).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A disc of moment of inertia 2 kg·m² rotates at 3 rad/s. Its rotational kinetic energy is:
questions.e: Kᵣot = ½Iω² = 0.5 × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at a small height h (h << R) above Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.e: gₕ = g/(1 + h/R)² ≈ g(1 − 2h/R) by binomial expansion for small h.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At a depth d below Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity becomes:
questions.e: Only the inner sphere of radius (R−d) attracts, giving gᵈ = g(1 − d/R) for uniform density.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The escape velocity from a planet depends on:
o: the mass of the projected body
the mass and radius of the planet only
questions.e: vₑ = √(2GM/R); it is independent of the mass or direction of the projected body.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A satellite of mass m in a circular orbit of radius r has total mechanical energy:
questions.e: K = +GMm/2r and U = −GMm/r, so E = K + U = −GMm/2r (bound orbit).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Kepler's third law of planetary motion states:
questions.e: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A geostationary satellite has a time period of:
questions.e: It must match Earth's rotation period (24 h) while orbiting in the equatorial plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The binding energy of a satellite of mass m in an orbit of radius r is:
questions.e: Binding energy = −(total energy) = GMm/2r, the energy needed to free it to infinity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Weightlessness is experienced during:
questions.e: In free fall both body and support accelerate at g, so the normal reaction (apparent weight) is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If Earth shrank to half its radius with unchanged mass, the surface gravity would become:
questions.e: g = GM/R² ∝ 1/R²; halving R multiplies g by four.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: The gravitational force between two masses follows the inverse-square law. Statement II: Gravitational potential energy is taken as zero at infinity.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: F = Gm₁m₂/r² and U = −Gm₁m₂/r → 0 as r → ∞; both are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The value of acceleration due to gravity at Earth's centre is:
questions.e: From gᵈ = g(1 − d/R), at d = R the effective attracting mass vanishes and g = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two satellites of masses m and 2m orbit Earth at the same radius. Their orbital speeds are in the ratio:
questions.e: v = √(GM/r) depends only on the planet's mass and orbital radius, not the satellite's mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vector of magnitude 10 units makes 60° with the x-axis. Its x-component is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dot product of two mutually perpendicular vectors is:
questions.e: A·B = AB cos90° = 0 for perpendicular vectors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body starts from rest and attains 30 m/s in 10 s with uniform acceleration. The distance covered is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): Friction always opposes the motion of a body. Reason (R): Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Friction can aid motion (walking, a driven car wheel); it opposes relative slipping, not motion itself, so A is false while R is true.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity η is:
questions.e: From F = ηA(dv/dx), [η] = [F]/[A][dv/dx] = MLT⁻²/(L²·T⁻¹) = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1000 kg car rounds an unbanked curve of radius 50 m. If μₛ = 0.4, the maximum safe speed is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.e: Friction provides centripetal force: vₘax = √(μₛrg) = √(0.4 × 50 × 10) = √200 = 10√2 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: A light year is a unit of distance. Statement II: A parsec is larger than a light year.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: A light year is the distance light travels in a year; one parsec ≈ 3.26 light years, so both statements hold.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics states that the heat supplied (ΔQ) equals:
questions.e: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW expresses conservation of energy: heat goes into internal energy and work done by the system.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an adiabatic process:
questions.e: Adiabatic means thermally insulated, so no heat is exchanged (Q = 0) and ΔU = −ΔW.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas:
questions.e: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, which is constant, so ΔU = 0 and Q = W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between 500 K and 300 K is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Mayer's relation for one mole of an ideal gas is:
questions.e: At constant pressure part of the heat does work, so Cₚ exceeds Cᵥ by the gas constant R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio γ = Cₚ/Cᵥ for a diatomic gas at room temperature is:
questions.e: A diatomic gas has 5 degrees of freedom: Cᵥ = 5R/2, Cₚ = 7R/2, so γ = 7/5 = 1.4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The root-mean-square speed of gas molecules is:
questions.e: From kinetic theory, cᵣms = √(3RT/M) = √(3kT/m).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The average kinetic energy per molecule of an ideal gas is:
questions.e: Each translational degree of freedom carries (1/2)kT; three of them give (3/2)kT per molecule.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): On a P–V diagram the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve. Reason (R): Adiabatic processes obey PV^γ = constant with γ > 1.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Slope of adiabat = −γP/V versus −P/V for isotherm; since γ > 1 the adiabatic is steeper, exactly as R states.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The net work done in a complete cyclic process equals:
o: the area enclosed by the cycle on the P–V diagram
questions.e: W = ∫PdV over the cycle is the enclosed area (positive for clockwise cycles).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which statement of the second law forbids 100% conversion of heat into work in a cyclic process?
questions.e: The Kelvin–Planck statement says no cyclic engine can convert heat from a single reservoir entirely into work.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: The entropy of the universe increases in every irreversible process. Statement II: A refrigerator moves heat from cold to hot at the cost of external work.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: Irreversible processes generate entropy (ΔSᵤniverse > 0), and refrigeration needs work input per the Clausius statement; both hold.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time period of a simple pendulum of length l is:
questions.e: For small oscillations T = 2π√(l/g), independent of the bob's mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration of the particle is maximum at the:
questions.e: a = −ω²y has maximum magnitude where displacement |y| = A, the extremes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The total mechanical energy of a particle executing SHM is proportional to the:
questions.e: E = ½kA², constant in time and scaling as A².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass m attached to a spring of constant k oscillates with frequency:
questions.e: f = ω/2π with ω = √(k/m).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is:
questions.e: v = √(tension/linear mass density) = √(T/μ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz sound together. The beat frequency heard is:
questions.e: Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂| = 4 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a stationary wave, the points of zero displacement are called:
questions.e: Nodes are permanent zero-displacement points; antinodes oscillate with maximum amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): A pendulum clock goes slow on a hot summer day. Reason (R): The effective length of the pendulum increases with temperature.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Thermal expansion lengthens the pendulum, and T = 2π√(l/g) rises, so the clock loses time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: Sound waves require a material medium for propagation. Statement II: Light waves are transverse electromagnetic waves.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave needing a medium; light is a transverse EM wave needing none.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Coulomb's law: the force between two point charges q₁ and q₂ separated by r is:
questions.e: F = (1/4πε₀)q₁q₂/r², an inverse-square law like gravitation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electrostatic field inside a hollow charged conductor is:
questions.e: In electrostatic equilibrium charges reside on the outer surface and the interior field cancels to zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electric field on the axial line of a short dipole at distance r is:
questions.e: Eₐxial = 2kp/r³, twice the equatorial field kp/r³ in magnitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The torque on an electric dipole of moment p in a uniform field E at angle θ is:
questions.e: τ = p × E has magnitude pE sinθ, tending to align the dipole with the field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The potential energy of a dipole held antiparallel to a uniform electric field is:
questions.e: U = −p·E = −pE cos180° = +pE, the maximum (unstable) energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is:
questions.e: C = ε₀A/d for plate area A and separation d (ignoring edge effects).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three 6 μF capacitors connected in series give an equivalent capacitance of:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electrostatic energy stored in a charged capacitor is:
questions.e: U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a dielectric slab of constant K is inserted between the plates of an isolated charged capacitor, its capacitance becomes:
questions.e: C = Kε₀A/d; the dielectric reduces the field, raising capacitance K-fold.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Gauss's law: the total electric flux through a closed surface equals:
questions.e: Φ = qₑnclosed/ε₀ regardless of the surface's shape or the charge distribution.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: Electric field lines never intersect each other. Statement II: Field lines start on positive charges and end on negative charges.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: Intersection would give two field directions at one point (impossible), and lines originate/terminate on charges as stated.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ohm's law is obeyed by:
questions.e: V = IR holds for ohmic (metallic) conductors at fixed temperature; diodes and electrolytes are non-ohmic.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistivity of a conductor depends on:
o: the nature of the material and its temperature
questions.e: Resistivity is a material property varying with temperature; length and area affect resistance, not resistivity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Resistors 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. The current through the 4 Ω resistor is:
questions.e: Each branch sees 12 V, so I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A through the 4 Ω resistor.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Kirchhoff's junction rule is a consequence of the conservation of:
questions.e: Charge cannot accumulate at a junction: incoming current equals outgoing current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge with arms P, Q, R, S, the condition is:
questions.e: Null deflection gives P/Q = R/S, used in the metre bridge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A potentiometer is preferred over a voltmeter for measuring EMF because at the null point it:
o: draws no current from the cell
questions.e: At balance no current flows through the cell, so the true EMF (not terminal voltage) is measured.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electrical power dissipated in a resistor is:
questions.e: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): The resistivity of metals increases with temperature. Reason (R): The collision frequency of electrons with lattice ions increases with temperature.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: More frequent collisions shorten the relaxation time τ, and ρ = m/ne²τ rises with temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter, one must connect:
questions.e: A shunt (low resistance) in parallel bypasses most current so the meter measures large currents safely.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop of radius R carrying current I is:
questions.e: From the Biot–Savart law, B = μ₀I/2R at the centre (times n for n turns).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field inside a long straight solenoid is:
questions.e: B = μ₀nI is uniform inside (n = turns per unit length) and nearly zero outside.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The force on a charge q moving with velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B is:
questions.e: F = qvB sinθ with θ = 90° gives qvB, perpendicular to both v and B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity. Its path is:
questions.e: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity, giving uniform circular motion (helical only if v has a parallel component).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The torque on a current-carrying loop in a magnetic field is maximum when the plane of the loop is:
questions.e: τ = NIAB sinθ (θ between normal and B) is maximum when the normal is perpendicular to B, i.e., the plane is parallel to B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic material is:
questions.e: Diamagnets are weakly repelled, with χ small and negative (e.g., bismuth, copper).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Curie temperature is the temperature above which a ferromagnetic material becomes:
questions.e: Thermal agitation destroys domain alignment above T_C, leaving paramagnetic behaviour.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: Isolated magnetic monopoles have never been observed. Statement II: Magnetic field lines always form closed loops.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: No monopoles are known, so ∇·B = 0 and field lines close on themselves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The induced EMF in a coil is 4 V when the current changes at 2 A/s. Its self-inductance is:
questions.e: e = L(dI/dt) gives L = 4/2 = 2 H.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The motional EMF developed in a rod of length l moving with speed v perpendicular to a field B is:
questions.e: e = Blv from the Lorentz force qvB separating charges along the rod.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The RMS value of an alternating current with peak value I₀ is:
questions.e: Iᵣms = I₀/√2 ≈ 0.707I₀ gives the same heating effect as DC.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At resonance in a series LCR circuit:
questions.e: Inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, impedance is minimum (R), current maximum and power factor unity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resonant frequency of an LC circuit is:
questions.e: Resonance when ωL = 1/ωC, so f = 1/(2π√(LC)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer works on the principle of:
questions.e: Changing flux in the primary induces EMF in the secondary: Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: Eddy-current losses in transformer cores are minimised with laminated cores. Statement II: A transformer cannot operate on DC supply.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: Laminations break eddy-current paths, and DC gives no changing flux, hence no induction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The correct order of increasing wavelength in the EM spectrum is:
o: radio waves, microwaves, IR, visible, UV, X-rays, γ-rays
X-rays, γ-rays, UV, visible, IR, radio waves, microwaves
visible, UV, IR, X-rays, γ-rays, microwaves, radio waves
γ-rays, X-rays, UV, visible, IR, microwaves, radio waves
questions.e: Wavelength increases from γ rays (~10⁻¹² m) to radio waves (~10³ m).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is:
questions.e: Maxwell's theory gives c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ozone layer primarily absorbs:
questions.e: Stratospheric ozone absorbs harmful UV-B/UV-C from the Sun.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Snell's law of refraction is:
o: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r
n₁ cos i = n₂ cos r
n₁ sin r = n₂ sin i
questions.e: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r relates the angles to the refractive indices of the two media.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels:
o: from denser to rarer medium with i greater than the critical angle
from denser to rarer with i less than the critical angle
questions.e: Both conditions — denser to rarer and i > iᶜ — are needed for TIR.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The critical angle for a medium of refractive index √2 is:
questions.e: sin iᶜ = 1/n = 1/√2 gives iᶜ = 45°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The power of a concave lens of focal length 50 cm is:
questions.e: P = 100/f(cm) = −100/50 = −2 dioptres (negative for concave).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a prism at the position of minimum deviation, the refracted ray inside the prism is:
questions.e: At δₘin the ray passes symmetrically, travelling parallel to the prism's base.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which colour of white light deviates most through a prism?
questions.e: Violet has the shortest wavelength and highest refractive index, hence maximum deviation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To increase the fringe width in Young's double-slit experiment, one should:
questions.e: β = λD/d, so fringe width grows with D and λ and shrinks with d.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The polarisation of light proves that light waves are:
questions.e: Only transverse waves can be polarised; longitudinal waves cannot.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons depends on the:
questions.e: Kₘax = hν − φ₀; intensity affects the number of electrons (photocurrent), not their energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The threshold frequency is the frequency below which:
questions.e: Photons below hν₀ = φ₀ cannot supply the work function, so no electrons are ejected.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of momentum p is:
questions.e: λ = h/p, verified by electron diffraction experiments.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Bohr's model, the angular momentum of an electron in the nth orbit is:
questions.e: Bohr's quantisation condition: mvr = nh/2π.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy of the electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom is:
questions.e: Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV; for n = 1 this is −13.6 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One atomic mass unit (1 u) is equivalent to:
questions.e: E = mc² for 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg gives about 931.5 MeV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assertion (A): Photoelectric emission occurs only above a threshold frequency. Reason (R): Each photon must supply at least the work-function energy to eject an electron.
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Einstein's equation Kₘax = hν − φ₀ requires hν ≥ φ₀; R is exactly why A holds.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Statement I: NAND and NOR gates are universal gates. Statement II: Doping silicon with phosphorus gives an n-type semiconductor.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: Any logic function can be built from NAND (or NOR) alone, and pentavalent P donates free electrons to Si.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of moles in 44 g of CO₂ is:
questions.e: Molar mass of CO₂ is 44 g/mol, so 44 g = 1 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Avogadro's number is:
questions.e: One mole contains 6.022 × 10²³ entities.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The empirical formula of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is:
questions.e: The simplest whole-number ratio of C:H:O is 1:2:1, i.e., CH₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Molarity is defined as:
o: moles of solute per kg of solvent
moles of solute per litre of solution
questions.e: Molarity = moles of solute / volume of solution in litres (temperature-dependent).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, if 4 g of H₂ reacts with 32 g of O₂, the limiting reagent is:
questions.e: 4 g H₂ = 2 mol needs exactly 1 mol O₂ = 32 g; the mixture is in exact stoichiometric ratio.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass of a single molecule of water is approximately:
questions.e: 18 g/mol ÷ 6.022 × 10²³ ≈ 3 × 10⁻²³ g per molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume occupied by one mole of any ideal gas at STP is:
questions.e: At STP (0°C, 1 atm) one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound contains 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O. Its empirical formula is:
questions.e: Mole ratio C:H:O = 3.33:6.7:3.33 = 1:2:1, giving CH₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiment established:
o: the nuclear model of the atom
questions.e: Large-angle scattering showed the positive charge concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The quantum numbers n = 2, l = 1 describe the:
questions.e: n = 2 with l = 1 (p) is the 2p subshell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of radial nodes in a 3p orbital is:
questions.e: Radial nodes = n − l − 1 = 3 − 1 − 1 = 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is:
questions.e: The half-filled 3d⁵ subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron shifts to 3d.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle relates the uncertainties in:
questions.e: Δx·Δp ≥ h/4π: position and momentum cannot both be known precisely.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The shape of a p-orbital is:
questions.e: p orbitals have two lobes (dumb-bell) with one angular node through the nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which set of quantum numbers is NOT possible?
questions.e: l must be less than n; l = 2 is not allowed for n = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assertion (A): In potassium the 4s orbital fills before 3d. Reason (R): For K, the 4s orbital lies lower in energy than 3d due to shielding (n+l rule).
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: The (n+l) rule gives 4s (4) below 3d (5); the configuration [Ar]4s¹ follows, explained by R.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Atomic radius generally, on moving left to right across a period:
questions.e: Increasing effective nuclear charge pulls the same shell closer, shrinking the atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The element with the highest electronegativity is:
questions.e: Fluorine (Pauling value 4.0) is the most electronegative element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The first ionisation enthalpy is highest for:
questions.e: Noble gases have stable closed shells and high effective nuclear charge, making electron removal hardest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions is the largest?
questions.e: Anion size increases down the group; iodide is the largest halide ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A diagonal relationship in the periodic table is shown by:
questions.e: Li resembles Mg diagonally (similar charge density), as do Be–Al and B–Si.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Statement I: The electron gain enthalpy of chlorine is more negative than that of fluorine. Statement II: The small size of fluorine causes strong electron–electron repulsion on adding an electron.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: Chlorine's larger 3p orbital accommodates the extra electron with less repulsion, so its electron gain enthalpy is more exothermic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The inert-pair effect is most prominent in:
o: heavier p-block elements such as Pb and Bi
questions.e: The ns² electrons resist ionisation in heavier p-block elements, stabilising lower oxidation states (Pb²⁺, Bi³⁺).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond order of the O₂⁺ ion is:
questions.e: O₂ has bond order 2; removing one antibonding π* electron raises it to 2.5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The shape of the methane molecule is:
questions.e: Four bond pairs with no lone pair on carbon give tetrahedral geometry (109.5°).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The hybridisation of carbon in ethene (C₂H₄) is:
questions.e: Each carbon forms three σ bonds (trigonal planar), leaving one p orbital for the π bond: sp².

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The dipole moment of NF₃ is non-zero because:
o: it has a pyramidal shape with a lone pair on nitrogen
fluorine is less electronegative than nitrogen
questions.e: Pyramidal geometry (one lone pair) prevents bond dipoles cancelling, unlike planar BF₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen bonding is strongest in:
questions.e: Fluorine is the most electronegative, giving the most polar H-bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to Fajans' rules, covalent character in an ionic compound increases with:
o: small cation, large anion and high charge
questions.e: High polarising power (small, highly charged cation) distorts the anion's electron cloud most.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond angle in the ammonia molecule is about:
questions.e: The lone pair compresses the tetrahedral angle to about 107° (pyramidal).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following species is paramagnetic?
questions.e: Molecular orbital theory places two unpaired electrons in O₂'s π* orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Statement I: Sigma bonds are stronger than π bonds. Statement II: Sigma bonds form by head-on overlap of orbitals.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: Head-on overlap gives greater electron density between nuclei, making σ bonds stronger than π bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The geometry of the XeF₂ molecule is:
questions.e: Five electron pairs (3 lone pairs) arrange trigonal-bipyramidally with lone pairs equatorial, leaving a linear molecule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its most stable form is:
questions.e: By convention Δ_fH° = 0 for elements in their standard states (e.g., O₂(g), C(graphite)).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a state function?
questions.e: Internal energy depends only on the state; work and heat are path functions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The entropy change is positive for:
questions.e: Melting increases disorder (solid → liquid), so ΔS > 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A process at constant temperature and pressure is spontaneous when:
questions.e: Negative Gibbs free energy change is the criterion for spontaneity at constant T and P.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hess's law of constant heat summation is an application of the:
questions.e: Enthalpy is a state function, so total ΔH is path-independent — energy conservation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assertion (A): The entropy of a perfectly crystalline solid is zero at 0 K. Reason (R): This is the statement of the third law of thermodynamics.
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.e: A perfect crystal at absolute zero has exactly one microstate (W = 1), so S = k ln W = 0 — the third law.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction with ΔH positive and ΔS positive, spontaneity occurs at:
questions.e: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS becomes negative only when T is large enough for TΔS to outweigh ΔH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), the relation between Kₚ and Kᶜ is:
questions.e: Kₚ = Kᶜ(RT)^Δn with Δn = 2 − 3 = −1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Increasing the pressure on the equilibrium N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ shifts it:
questions.e: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (2 vs 4): ammonia formation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ionic product of water K_w at 25°C is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a 0.001 M NaOH solution is:
questions.e: [OH⁻] = 10⁻³ gives pOH = 3, so pH = 14 − 3 = 11.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A buffer solution, which resists pH change, consists of:
o: a salt of a strong acid only
a weak acid and its conjugate base
a weak acid and a strong acid
a strong acid and a strong base
questions.e: The conjugate pair (e.g., CH₃COOH/CH₃COO⁻) neutralises added H⁺ or OH⁻.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of AgCl decreases on adding NaCl due to the:
questions.e: Added Cl⁻ shifts AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ left, lowering solubility (Le Chatelier).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a sparingly soluble salt AₓB_y, the solubility product Kₛp equals:
questions.e: For AₓB_y ⇌ xA + yB, Kₛp = [A]ˣ[B]ʸ with stoichiometric exponents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Statement I: A catalyst does not change the equilibrium constant of a reaction. Statement II: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both forward and reverse reactions.
o: Both I and II are false
Both I and II are true
questions.e: Catalysts speed up both directions equally, so K is unchanged while Eₐ falls for both.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of sulphur in H₂SO₄ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a disproportionation reaction?
questions.e: Cl₂ (0) is simultaneously oxidised to ClO⁻ (+1) and reduced to Cl⁻ (−1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The strongest oxidising agent among the halogens is:
questions.e: Fluorine has the highest standard reduction potential, making F₂ the strongest oxidiser.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the electrochemical series, metals placed above hydrogen:
questions.e: They have negative E° and reduce H⁺ to H₂ from dilute acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the half-reaction MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ (acidic medium), the number of electrons gained per Mn is:
questions.e: Mn goes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Statement I: Oxidation is the loss of electrons. Statement II: Reducing agents themselves get oxidised.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.e: OILRIG: oxidation is loss; the reductant donates electrons and is oxidised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a Daniel cell, the anode is the:
questions.e: Oxidation (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻) occurs at the anode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a potential of:
questions.e: SHE is the reference electrode with E° ≡ 0.00 V at all temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Nernst equation for the reduction Mⁿ⁺ + ne⁻ → M is:
questions.e: E = E° − (0.0591/n) log(Q) at 298 K with Q = 1/[Mⁿ⁺].

questions.subject: Chemistry
