questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The deuteron has a binding energy of 2.2 MeV. Its mass defect is approximately:
questions.e: Mass defect Δm = BE/c² = 2.2 MeV / 931.5 MeV per u ≈ 0.00236 u.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a magic number for nuclear stability?
questions.e: Nuclei with 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82 or 126 protons or neutrons show extra stability; 82 is the magic proton number of lead.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The density of nuclear matter is:
o: proportional to the cube root of the mass number
inversely proportional to the mass number
approximately independent of the mass number
questions.e: Since nuclear volume scales with A (R ∝ A^(1/3)) and mass also scales with A, the density is nearly the same for all nuclei, about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For stable heavy nuclei, the neutron-to-proton ratio N/Z is approximately:
questions.e: Light stable nuclei have N ≈ Z, but heavy stable nuclei need extra neutrons to dilute proton–proton repulsion, settling near N/Z ≈ 1.5 along the band of stability.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: After three half-lives, the fraction of the original sample that has decayed is:
questions.e: The undecayed fraction after 3 half-lives is (1/2)³ = 1/8, so the decayed fraction is 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The forbidden energy gap of germanium at room temperature is approximately:
questions.e: Germanium has a band gap of about 0.72 eV, smaller than silicon's 1.1 eV, which is why germanium devices leak more at higher temperatures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Doping pure silicon with phosphorus (a pentavalent impurity) produces:
questions.e: Phosphorus contributes a free fifth electron, making electrons the majority carriers, so the material becomes n-type.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The barrier potential of a silicon p–n junction at room temperature is about:
questions.e: The built-in potential across a silicon junction is roughly 0.6–0.7 V (about 0.3 V for germanium), arising from ionised dopants in the depletion region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a p–n junction is forward biased, the width of the depletion region:
o: becomes equal to the junction length
questions.e: Forward bias pushes majority carriers toward the junction, neutralising the exposed ions and narrowing the depletion layer, which lowers the barrier.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A half-wave rectifier uses:
questions.e: Half-wave rectification passes only one half-cycle of the AC input, which a single diode in series can achieve; full-wave designs need two or four.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light-emitting diodes are commonly fabricated from:
questions.e: LEDs need direct-band-gap materials for efficient photon emission; gallium arsenide and gallium phosphide are standard choices, while silicon is indirect-gap and a poor emitter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For an n–p–n transistor operating in the active mode:
o: emitter–base is reverse biased and collector–base is forward biased
emitter–base is forward biased and collector–base is reverse biased
questions.e: Active-mode amplification needs the emitter–base junction forward biased (to inject carriers) and the collector–base junction reverse biased (to collect them).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transistor has current gain β = 99. Its common-base current gain α is:
questions.e: α = β/(β + 1) = 99/100 = 0.99, always just below unity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which pair of logic gates is universal, i.e. can realise any Boolean function?
questions.e: NAND and NOR are each functionally complete: NOT, AND and OR can all be built from either one alone.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Zener diode is primarily used as a:
questions.e: Operated in reverse breakdown, a Zener diode holds a nearly constant voltage across itself, making it a simple voltage regulator.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A photodiode is normally operated in:
questions.e: Reverse bias widens the depletion region so incoming photons generate a photocurrent that adds to the small reverse saturation current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electrical conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor as temperature rises:
questions.e: Heating breaks more covalent bonds, creating more electron–hole pairs, so conductivity rises — the opposite behaviour to metals.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A NAND gate with both inputs HIGH produces an output that is:
questions.e: NAND is AND followed by NOT: HIGH AND HIGH is HIGH, and the inversion makes it LOW.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The depletion region of a p–n junction contains:
questions.e: Mobile carriers have diffused away, leaving behind fixed ionised dopant atoms — positive donors on the n-side and negative acceptors on the p-side.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the pressure exerted by an ideal gas equals:
questions.e: Molecular bombardment of the walls gives p = (1/3)nm⟨v²⟩, which is one-third the density times the mean-square speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At the same temperature, the ratio of the rms speed of helium molecules to that of oxygen molecules is:
questions.e: v_rms ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(M_O₂/M_He) = √(32/4) = √8 ≈ 2.83.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The number of degrees of freedom of a diatomic gas molecule at room temperature is:
questions.e: A diatomic molecule has 3 translational and 2 rotational degrees of freedom active at room temperature (vibration is frozen out), giving 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The internal energy of one mole of a monoatomic ideal gas at absolute temperature T is:
questions.e: With 3 translational degrees of freedom and (1/2)RT per mole per degree, U = (3/2)RT.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of specific heats γ = Cp/Cv for a monoatomic ideal gas is:
questions.e: For a monoatomic gas Cv = (3/2)R and Cp = (5/2)R, so γ = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mean free path of gas molecules increases when the:
o: volume is decreased at constant temperature
questions.e: Mean free path λ = 1/(√2 nπd²) is inversely proportional to the number density, so lowering the pressure (fewer molecules per unit volume) lengthens it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the root-mean-square speed to the most probable speed of gas molecules is:
questions.e: v_rms = √(3RT/M) and v_mp = √(2RT/M), so v_rms/v_mp = √(3/2) ≈ 1.225.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The molar specific heat at constant volume of a diatomic ideal gas at room temperature is:
questions.e: Five active degrees of freedom give Cv = (5/2)R per mole, with Cp = (7/2)R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rms speed of nitrogen molecules at 300 K is closest to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The law of equipartition of energy assigns to each quadratic degree of freedom an average energy of:
questions.e: Every term quadratic in a coordinate or momentum contributes (1/2)kT per molecule at thermal equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Real gases deviate most from ideal behaviour at:
questions.e: High pressure shrinks intermolecular spacing (finite molecular volume matters) and low temperature lets attractive forces dominate, both breaking ideal-gas assumptions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: As the temperature of a gas is raised, the peak of the Maxwell speed distribution:
o: shifts to lower speeds and grows taller
stays at the same speed but broadens
shifts to higher speeds and becomes lower
questions.e: The most probable speed √(2RT/M) moves right with temperature, and since the total area (number of molecules) is fixed, the peak height falls.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Dalton's law of partial pressures states that the total pressure of a gas mixture equals:
o: the average of the partial pressures
the sum of the partial pressures of the components
the pressure of the heaviest component
the product of the partial pressures
questions.e: Each gas exerts the pressure it would exert alone in the same volume, and these partial pressures add up to the measured total.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnitude of the emf induced in a coil is directly proportional to the:
o: rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil
square of the number of turns
questions.e: Faraday's law gives ε = −N(dΦ/dt): the induced emf scales with how fast the flux changes, not with the flux itself.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Lenz's law determines the:
questions.e: The minus sign in Faraday's law is Lenz's law: the induced current flows so that its magnetic effect opposes the change in flux that produced it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 m rod moves at 10 m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.5 T field, with its length perpendicular to both velocity and field. The motional emf is:
questions.e: Motional emf ε = Blv = 0.5 × 2 × 10 = 10 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solenoid has 500 turns, cross-sectional area 10 cm² and length 50 cm. Its self-inductance is about:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy stored in a 2 H inductor carrying 3 A is:
questions.e: Magnetic energy U = (1/2)LI² = 0.5 × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Eddy current losses in a transformer core are minimised by using a:
questions.e: Thin insulated laminations break up the large circulating eddy-current loops into tiny ones, greatly raising the effective resistance to them.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an AC generator, the induced emf is maximum when the plane of the rotating coil is:
questions.e: ε = NBAω sin ωt is largest when the coil's normal is perpendicular to the field, i.e. when the plane of the coil lies parallel to the field lines and flux is changing fastest.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When the magnetic flux through a loop of resistance R changes by ΔΦ, the total charge that flows is:
questions.e: Since I = ε/R = (1/R)(dΦ/dt), integrating over time gives q = ΔΦ/R — independent of how quickly the change happens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer works on:
questions.e: Transformer action needs a continuously changing flux to induce the secondary emf, so it operates on alternating current only.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time constant of a series LR circuit is:
questions.e: Current grows as I = I₀(1 − e^(−Rt/L)), so the characteristic time for the rise is L/R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The north pole of a bar magnet approaches a circular loop. Viewed from the magnet side, the induced current is:
questions.e: By Lenz's law the loop's near face must act as a north pole to repel the approaching magnet, and a north pole is produced by an anticlockwise current viewed from that side.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula of mutual inductance is:
questions.e: Inductance has the dimensions of (energy)/(current)² = [ML²T⁻²]/[A²] = [ML²T⁻²A⁻²], the henry.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The self-induced emf in a coil opposes the:
questions.e: Self-induction is Lenz's law applied to a coil's own field: the induced emf always fights any rise or fall of the current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, the fringe width β is given by:
questions.e: Fringe width β = λD/d grows with wavelength and screen distance and shrinks as the slits move apart.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When white light is used in Young's double-slit experiment, the central fringe is:
questions.e: At the centre the path difference is zero for every wavelength, so all colours reinforce and the central maximum appears white, with coloured fringes on either side.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For sustained interference, the two sources must be:
o: coherent, with a constant phase difference
questions.e: Only coherent sources — same frequency and a phase difference constant in time — keep the interference pattern stationary.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a single-slit diffraction pattern, the first minimum occurs at an angle θ satisfying:
questions.e: The path difference between rays from opposite edges of a slit of width a is a sin θ; destructive interference first occurs when this equals one wavelength.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Unpolarised light of intensity I₀ passes through a single ideal polariser. The transmitted intensity is:
questions.e: Averaging Malus's law over all random polarisation directions halves the intensity: ⟨cos²θ⟩ = 1/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Brewster's angle i_p for a medium of refractive index μ satisfies:
questions.e: At Brewster's angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, giving tan i_p = μ and completely polarised reflected light.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light of intensity I₀ passes through two crossed polaroids with a third polaroid at 45° between them. The final intensity is:
questions.e: After the first polaroid the intensity is I₀/2; the 45° polaroid transmits (I₀/2)cos²45° = I₀/4; the last, crossed with the first, transmits (I₀/4)cos²45° = I₀/8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The reddish appearance of the Sun at sunrise and sunset is due to:
questions.e: Rayleigh scattering removes short (blue) wavelengths from the long atmospheric path, leaving the transmitted red light dominant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resolving power of a telescope increases when the:
questions.e: Resolving power = D/(1.22λ), so a larger objective diameter directly improves the ability to separate close objects.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A path difference of one wavelength corresponds to a phase difference of:
questions.e: Phase difference Δφ = (2π/λ) × path difference, so one full wavelength gives 2π radians.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Colours seen in a thin oil film in sunlight are explained by:
o: interference of light reflected from the two surfaces
questions.e: Rays reflected from the top and bottom of the thin film interfere; the condition depends on wavelength, so different colours reinforce at different thicknesses.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Huygens' principle treats every point on a wavefront as:
questions.e: Each point on a wavefront acts as a fresh source of spherical secondary wavelets, whose envelope forms the new wavefront.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the Doppler effect for light, the red shift of distant galaxies indicates that they are:
questions.e: Receding sources stretch the observed wavelength toward the red end; the cosmological red shift shows the universe is expanding.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Bohr's model, the radius of the n-th orbit of hydrogen is proportional to:
questions.e: Quantised angular momentum gives r_n = n²h²ε₀/(πme²) = 0.53n² Å, growing as the square of the principal quantum number.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy of the electron in the second excited state (n = 3) of hydrogen is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The spectral series of hydrogen that lies in the visible region is the:
questions.e: Transitions ending at n = 2 (Balmer) emit visible photons such as Hα at 656 nm; Lyman is ultraviolet and the rest are infrared.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the radius of the second Bohr orbit to the first is:
questions.e: Since r_n ∝ n², r₂/r₁ = 2²/1² = 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Using the Rydberg formula, the wavelength of the Lyman-alpha line (2 → 1) is about:
questions.e: 1/λ = R(1/1 − 1/4) = 3R/4 with R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹ gives λ ≈ 121.5 nm, in the ultraviolet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angular momentum of the electron in the third Bohr orbit of hydrogen is:
questions.e: Bohr's condition L = nh/2π gives L = 3h/2π for n = 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The red Hα line of the Balmer series (n = 3 → 2) has a wavelength of about:
questions.e: The 3 → 2 transition releases 1.89 eV, corresponding to λ = hc/E ≈ 656 nm in the red.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ionisation energy of hydrogen in its ground state is:
questions.e: Removing the electron from n = 1 to infinity needs 0 − (−13.6 eV) = 13.6 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Alpha particles scattering off gold foil in Rutherford's experiment showed that:
o: atoms are mostly empty space with a tiny dense nucleus
questions.e: Most alpha particles passed through undeflected while a few bounced back, proving the positive charge and mass sit in a nucleus about 10⁻¹⁴ m across inside a 10⁻¹⁰ m atom.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 100 V is about:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Franck–Hertz experiment provided direct evidence for:
questions.e: Electrons lost energy to mercury atoms only in discrete 4.9 eV steps, showing atoms absorb energy in quanta.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Dark lines in the solar absorption spectrum are produced when:
o: cooler gases above the photosphere absorb specific wavelengths
the photosphere emits at all wavelengths
questions.e: Fraunhofer lines appear where atoms in the Sun's cooler outer layers absorb their characteristic wavelengths from the continuous spectrum below.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Moseley's law relates the frequency of characteristic X-rays to the:
questions.e: √ν = a(Z − b): the Kα frequency scales with (Z − 1)², which is how Moseley ordered the periodic table by atomic number.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum, the ratio of the electric field amplitude to the magnetic field amplitude is:
questions.e: Maxwell's equations give E₀/B₀ = c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following has the longest wavelength?
questions.e: The spectrum runs γ < X-ray < UV < visible < IR < microwave < radio in increasing wavelength; radio waves reach metres to kilometres.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Microwave ovens heat food mainly because microwaves:
o: are absorbed by water, fats and sugars, making polar molecules rotate
questions.e: Oven magnetrons emit ~2.45 GHz radiation that couples to the rotation of polar molecules, especially water, generating heat by molecular friction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ozone layer protects life by absorbing:
questions.e: Ozone strongly absorbs UV-B and UV-C, shielding surface life from their DNA-damaging effects.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which property proves that electromagnetic waves are transverse?
questions.e: Only transverse waves can be polarised; longitudinal waves like sound show interference and diffraction too.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Displacement current was introduced by Maxwell to:
o: make Ampère's law consistent with charge conservation in a charging capacitor
questions.e: Between capacitor plates there is no conduction current, but the changing electric flux ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) acts as a current source for the magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Hertz's spark-gap experiment is historically important because it:
o: first generated and detected radio waves
questions.e: Hertz produced electromagnetic waves with an oscillating spark discharge and detected them metres away, confirming Maxwell's prediction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The frequency of electromagnetic waves produced by an LC circuit is:
questions.e: The natural oscillation frequency of an inductor–capacitor circuit is f = 1/(2π√(LC)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Infrared radiation is used in:
questions.e: IR is emitted by warm bodies and used in TV remotes, night-vision and thermal cameras; sterilisation uses UV and imaging uses X-rays.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave carries momentum, which means it can exert:
questions.e: Photons carry momentum p = E/c, so absorbed or reflected light pushes on surfaces — the basis of solar sails.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The visible spectrum spans approximately:
questions.e: Human vision covers roughly 4000–7000 Å (violet to red); beyond lie ultraviolet and infrared.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Greenhouse warming by the atmosphere is mainly due to absorption of:
o: outgoing infrared by CO₂ and water vapour
questions.e: The surface radiates heat as infrared, which greenhouse gases absorb and re-radiate downward, keeping the Earth warmer than it would otherwise be.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stretched string has tension T and mass per unit length μ. If the tension is doubled and the mass per unit length is also doubled, the transverse wave speed:
questions.e: v = √(T/μ); doubling both numerator and denominator leaves the ratio — and hence the speed — unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a stationary wave, the distance between two consecutive nodes is:
questions.e: Nodes repeat every half wavelength: the fundamental mode of a string fixed at both ends fits exactly λ/2 between the ends.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tuning fork of frequency 512 Hz produces 6 beats per second when sounded with another fork. The frequency of the second fork could be:
questions.e: Beat frequency is the magnitude of the difference, so the unknown fork is 512 ± 6 Hz, i.e. 506 Hz or 518 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A closed organ pipe of length L sounding its fundamental has a wavelength of:
questions.e: The closed end is a node and the open end an antinode, so L = λ/4 and λ = 4L; only odd harmonics sound.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of sound in air increases by about 0.61 m/s for every:
questions.e: v ∝ √T, giving roughly +0.61 m/s per degree Celsius near room temperature (about 343 m/s at 20°C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train sounding a 400 Hz whistle approaches a stationary observer at 30 m/s (sound speed 330 m/s). The observed frequency is about:
questions.e: For an approaching source f′ = f·v/(v − v_s) = 400 × 330/300 = 440 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The loudness of sound is measured in:
questions.e: Loudness level uses the decibel scale, which is logarithmic in intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The fundamental frequency of a stretched string of length L, tension T and mass per unit length μ is:
questions.e: The fundamental fits half a wavelength in the string (λ = 2L), so f = v/λ = (1/2L)√(T/μ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sound waves cannot travel through vacuum because they are:
o: mechanical waves needing a material medium
questions.e: Sound is a pressure disturbance passed from particle to particle; with no particles there is nothing to carry it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two waves of the same frequency differ in phase by π. Their interference is:
questions.e: A phase difference of π (half a wavelength path difference) makes crest meet trough, giving destructive interference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of incident light (above threshold frequency) increases the:
o: number of photoelectrons emitted per second
questions.e: More photons knock out more electrons (higher photocurrent), but each electron's energy hν − φ₀ depends only on frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Einstein's photoelectric equation is:
questions.e: A photon's energy splits into the work function needed to escape plus the electron's leftover kinetic energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The slope of the stopping-potential versus frequency graph in the photoelectric effect equals:
questions.e: From eV₀ = hν − φ₀, V₀ = (h/e)ν − φ₀/e, so the slope is h/e and the intercept gives the work function.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass m and kinetic energy K is:
questions.e: With p = √(2mK), λ = h/p = h/√(2mK).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Davisson–Germer experiment confirmed the:
questions.e: Electrons scattered off a nickel crystal showed a diffraction maximum, proving matter waves with λ = h/p.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Photoelectric emission occurs only if the incident frequency is:
questions.e: Electrons escape only when hν ≥ φ₀, i.e. ν ≥ ν₀; no intensity of lower-frequency light can compensate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The stopping potential in a photoelectric experiment measures the:
o: maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons
questions.e: The retarding voltage that just halts the fastest electrons satisfies eV₀ = K_max.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Matter waves are:
o: probability waves associated with moving particles
questions.e: The de Broglie wave's amplitude squared gives the probability of finding the particle; it is neither an EM wave nor a mechanical vibration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the Compton effect, the wavelength of scattered X-rays:
questions.e: The photon loses energy to the electron, so λ′ − λ = (h/mc)(1 − cosθ) > 0 and the scattered wavelength grows.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The momentum of a photon of wavelength λ is:
questions.e: From E = hc/λ = pc, the photon momentum is p = h/λ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass m on a spring of constant k oscillates with period:
questions.e: From ω = √(k/m), T = 2π/ω = 2π√(m/k).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the speed is maximum at the:
questions.e: v = ω√(A² − x²) peaks at x = 0 where all the energy is kinetic.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The total mechanical energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is proportional to the:
questions.e: E = (1/2)kA² = (1/2)mω²A², fixed by the amplitude squared.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A second's pendulum has a time period of 2 s. Its length is approximately:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a sinusoidal current I = I₀ sin ωt, the rms value is:
questions.e: Averaging sin² over a cycle gives 1/2, so I_rms = I₀/√2 ≈ 0.707I₀.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a series LCR circuit, resonance occurs when:
questions.e: At ω₀ = 1/√(LC) the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, impedance is minimum (equal to R) and current is maximum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The average power dissipated in a purely inductive AC circuit over a full cycle is:
questions.e: Voltage and current are 90° out of phase, so P = V_rms I_rms cos 90° = 0 — a wattless current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A step-up transformer has a turns ratio N_s/N_p = 10. If the primary voltage is 220 V, the secondary voltage is:
questions.e: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p gives V_s = 10 × 220 = 2200 V.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which lanthanoid most readily exhibits the +4 oxidation state?
questions.e: Cerium attains the noble-gas configuration [Xe] as Ce⁴⁺, so the +4 state is uniquely accessible and strongly oxidising.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ionic radius of Lu³⁺ compared to that of La³⁺ is:
questions.e: Lanthanoid contraction shrinks the ions steadily across the series, so lutetium(III) is markedly smaller than lanthanum(III).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction is that:
o: zirconium and hafnium have nearly identical atomic radii
questions.e: The contraction accumulated across the 4f series cancels the normal size increase down the group, making the 4d/5d pair Zr/Hf almost the same size and chemically similar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ce⁴⁺ in aqueous solution is a:
questions.e: Ce⁴⁺ (E° = +1.74 V for the Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺ couple) has a strong drive to gain an electron and revert to the common +3 state of the lanthanoids, so it oxidises even water and is a powerful oxidant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The only radioactive lanthanoid is:
questions.e: Promethium (Z = 61) has no stable isotope; all other lanthanoids occur with at least one stable isotope.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Actinoid contraction is greater than lanthanoid contraction because:
o: 5f electrons shield even more poorly than 4f
questions.e: The more diffuse 5f orbitals screen the nuclear charge even less effectively than 4f, so the size decrease per element is steeper across the actinoids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Misch metal, used in lighter flints, consists of:
o: 95% lanthanoid metals + 5% iron with traces of S, C, Ca and Al
questions.e: This pyrophoric alloy is mostly a lanthanoid mixture with iron and small amounts of sulphur, carbon, calcium and aluminium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The magnetic moment of Gd³⁺ (4f⁷) is approximately:
questions.e: With 7 unpaired electrons, μ = √[n(n+2)] = √63 ≈ 7.94 BM, the highest spin-only value in the lanthanoid series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of lanthanoid ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.e: Colour comes from f–f transitions; La³⁺ (f⁰) and Lu³⁺ (f¹⁴) have no possible f–f jump and are colourless.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The maximum oxidation state exhibited by the actinoids is:
questions.e: Early actinoids reach high states — neptunium and plutonium attain +7 — unlike lanthanoids which stay near +3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Eu²⁺ is a strong reducing agent because:
o: it is oxidised to Eu³⁺, the common +3 state, driven by the large hydration energy of the small Eu³⁺ ion
questions.e: Oxidation of Eu²⁺ gives Eu³⁺, the normal lanthanoid state; the highly charged Eu³⁺ ion is enormously stabilised by hydration, so Eu²⁺ readily donates its electron to other species.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lanthanoids are separated from one another industrially by:
questions.e: Their nearly identical sizes and chemistry defeat ordinary methods; ion-exchange resins exploit the tiny radius differences across the series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a lanthanoid?
questions.e: The lanthanoid series runs from cerium (58) to lutetium (71); actinium (89) heads the actinoid series instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a transition element?
questions.e: Zinc has a complete d¹⁰ configuration both as metal and as Zn²⁺, so by definition it is not a transition element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The highest oxidation state shown by manganese is:
questions.e: In permanganate (MnO₄⁻) manganese is +7, using all seven 3d⁵4s² electrons in bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The blue colour of aqueous Cu²⁺ salts is due to:
questions.e: Absorption of visible light promotes a 3d electron between split d-orbitals, and the transmitted colour appears blue.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of Fe³⁺ (3d⁵) is approximately:
questions.e: Five unpaired electrons give μ = √[5(5+2)] = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises a reducing agent, the observed colour change is:
questions.e: Dichromate (Cr⁶⁺, orange) is reduced to Cr³⁺ (green), a classic test-tube observation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The catalyst used in Haber's process for ammonia synthesis is:
questions.e: Finely divided iron (with Mo promoter) catalyses N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ at high pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Brass is an alloy of:
questions.e: Brass is Cu–Zn; bronze is Cu–Sn and steel is Fe–C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: KMnO₄ can act as its own indicator in redox titrations because:
o: MnO₄⁻ is intensely purple while Mn²⁺ is almost colourless
questions.e: The disappearance of the purple colour marks the end point without any external indicator.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.e: Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰ with no d–d transition possible; the others have partially filled d shells and are coloured.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an interstitial compound?
questions.e: Small carbon atoms occupy interstitial sites in the titanium lattice in TiC, giving extreme hardness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The highest oxidation state known (+8) is shown by osmium in:
questions.e: Osmium tetroxide contains Os(VIII), the maximum oxidation state exhibited by any element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Scandium exhibits only the +3 oxidation state because:
o: removing 4s²3d¹ leaves the stable noble-gas configuration
it has a very high ionisation enthalpy
questions.e: Sc ([Ar]3d¹4s²) loses all three outer electrons to reach argon's configuration; removing more would break a noble-gas core.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which is the strongest acid among the following?
questions.e: The electron-withdrawing chlorine stabilises the carboxylate by the −I effect; Ka runs ClCH₂COOH (1.4×10⁻³) > HCOOH > C₆H₅COOH > CH₃COOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction converts a carboxylic acid into its:
questions.e: Treatment with Cl₂ or Br₂ in the presence of red phosphorus halogenates the alpha carbon selectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sodium acetate heated with soda lime gives:
questions.e: Decarboxylation (RCOONa + NaOH → RH + Na₂CO₃) removes CO₂, converting acetate to methane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Reduction of a carboxylic acid with LiAlH₄ yields a:
questions.e: Lithium aluminium hydride reduces the −COOH group all the way to −CH₂OH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Formic acid gives a positive Tollens' test because it:
o: forms a silver mirror by reduction
is oxidised to CO₂, behaving like an aldehyde
questions.e: The aldehydic hydrogen of HCOOH is oxidised by Tollens' reagent to carbonate while silver deposits as the mirror.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of increasing acid strength is:
questions.e: Acid strength follows the −I power of the halogen: F > Cl > Br > I, so fluoroacetic acid is the strongest of the four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Esterification of acetic acid with ethanol is carried out in the presence of:
questions.e: Fischer esterification is acid-catalysed; concentrated sulphuric acid also absorbs the water formed, driving the equilibrium toward the ester.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Malonic acid (HOOC–CH₂–COOH) on heating gives:
questions.e: 1,3-dicarboxylic acids decarboxylate on heating, losing one CO₂ to give the monocarboxylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct decreasing order of acid strength is:
questions.e: Formic acid (no electron-donating alkyl group) beats benzoic acid, which in turn beats acetic acid whose methyl group donates electrons by +I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols mainly because:
o: the carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance over two equivalent oxygens
questions.e: The negative charge in RCOO⁻ is delocalised equally over two oxygens, a stabilisation the phenoxide ion (charge spread into the ring but still localised on one oxygen) cannot match.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because:
o: its glycosidic bond joins the anomeric carbons of both units, leaving no free aldehyde or ketone
questions.e: In sucrose the C1 of glucose links to the C2 of fructose, so neither reducing end survives and Fehling's or Tollens' tests stay negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a DNA sample, adenine constitutes 20% of the bases. The percentage of guanine is:
questions.e: By Chargaff's rule A = T = 20%, so G = C = (100 − 40)/2 = 30%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A peptide bond is best described as:
o: an ionic link between amino acids
an amide linkage formed between —COOH and —NH₂ with loss of water
questions.e: Condensation of the carboxyl group of one amino acid with the amino group of the next creates the —CO—NH— backbone of proteins.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Deficiency of vitamin D in children causes:
questions.e: Without vitamin D, calcium absorption and bone mineralisation fail, softening growing bones into rickets.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The basic unit of biological classification is the:
questions.e: Species is the lowest and fundamental taxonomic rank; all higher categories are built by grouping species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Binomial nomenclature was proposed by:
questions.e: Linnaeus introduced the genus + species naming system in Species Plantarum (1753).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct ascending order of taxonomic categories is:
o: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Genus → Family → Species
Species → Family → Genus → Class → Order → Phylum → Kingdom
Genus → Species → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
questions.e: Categories widen upward: species, genus, family, order, class, phylum (division in plants), kingdom.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Systematics, as distinct from taxonomy, additionally includes the study of:
questions.e: Simpson defined systematics as taxonomy plus the evolutionary history connecting the taxa.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A herbarium is a:
o: storehouse of dried, pressed and preserved plant specimens on sheets
collection of living plants in a garden
questions.e: Herbarium sheets carry dried specimens with labels of date, place and collector for taxonomic reference.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The largest botanical garden in the world is:
questions.e: Kew in England holds the world's largest living and preserved plant collections.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The Indian Botanical Garden is located at:
questions.e: Founded in 1787 at Shibpur, Howrah, it houses the famous Great Banyan Tree.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a taxonomic key, a pair of contrasting characters is called a:
questions.e: Each couplet offers two opposing statements; choosing one leads to the next until the taxon is identified.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Zoological parks are an example of:
questions.e: Keeping animals outside their natural habitat for protection, breeding and study is ex-situ conservation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The term 'flora' refers to the:
questions.e: Flora lists the plants of an area; fauna lists its animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The International Code of Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN) is now known as the:
questions.e: It was renamed the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (ICN).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In museums, insects are preserved in:
questions.e: Insects are killed, pinned and stored dry in insect boxes; larger animals go into jars with preservative solutions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The most abundant protein in the world is:
questions.e: RuBisCO, the carbon-fixing enzyme of photosynthesis, is present in every green leaf and outweighs all other proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The most abundant organic compound on Earth is:
questions.e: Cellulose in plant cell walls exceeds every other organic substance in total mass.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Inulin, a fructan storage carbohydrate, is found in the roots of:
questions.e: Dahlia tubers store inulin instead of starch, a classic NCERT example.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following amino acids is essential for humans?
questions.e: Valine cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from diet; glycine, alanine and serine are non-essential.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Qdenga (TAK-003), the first dengue vaccine approved by India's CDSCO, is best described as:
o: a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine against all four dengue serotypes
an inactivated monovalent vaccine against DENV-2 only
an mRNA vaccine encoding the dengue NS1 protein
a toxoid-based vaccine targeting Aedes saliva proteins
questions.e: Qdenga is a live-attenuated vaccine built on a DENV-2 backbone covering DENV-1 to DENV-4; CDSCO cleared it in July 2026 for ages 4–60, given as two doses three months apart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the September 2026 engineered-probiotic study, the enzyme cytosine deaminase produced by E. coli inside tumours converts the non-toxic prodrug 5-FC into:
questions.e: 5-FC (5-fluorocytosine) stays harmless until cytosine deaminase converts it to 5-FU, a cytotoxic chemotherapy drug, right inside the tumour; the bacteria also co-delivered an IL-15 superagonist and a PD-L1-blocking nanobody.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: MFSD2B, whose S1P-bound structure was resolved by cryo-EM in September 2026, is a transporter found mainly in red blood cells and platelets that exports which signalling lipid into the blood?
questions.e: S1P keeps blood vessels healthy and guides immune-cell movement, but cannot cross membranes freely; MFSD2B acts as its gateway out of RBCs and platelets.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: BC200, a human noncoding RNA recently reported integrated into the genome of a poxvirus, exemplifies which class of genetic elements?
questions.e: BC200 is a primate-specific transposable element enriched in neurons; its capture by molluscum contagiosum virus is the first clear wild case of a vertebrate transposon jumping into a virus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: According to a September 2026 study published in Nature, the cohesin complex helps prevent errors during DNA replication by:
o: adding nucleotides to the leading strand
reshaping replication-fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal
removing Okazaki fragments from the lagging strand
unwinding the parental DNA double helix
questions.e: Cohesin rings hold sister chromatids together and remodel stalled replication forks, protecting against replication stress and DNA damage — relevant to precision oncology since cohesin is mutated in several cancers.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward with speed 20 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and neglecting air resistance, the maximum height it reaches is:
questions.e: At maximum height v = 0, so h = u²/2g = (20)²/(2 × 10) = 400/20 = 20 m.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the titration of oxalic acid against acidified KMnO₄, the oxidation state of manganese changes from:
questions.e: In acidic medium the permanganate ion MnO₄⁻ (+7) is reduced to Mn²⁺ (+2) — a five-electron change; the disappearance of the purple colour makes KMnO₄ a self-indicator.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: pTOS (para-tyramine-O-sulfate), the appetite-suppressing compound discovered in python blood in September 2026, contains which functional group?
questions.e: pTOS is tyramine esterified with sulfate at the phenolic oxygen — an aryl sulfate ester — and it suppresses appetite by acting on the brain's regulatory centre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work done in moving a charge of 2 C across a potential difference of 12 V is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm forms an image 30 cm in front of the mirror. The object distance is:
questions.e: Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives 1/15 = 1/30 + 1/u, so 1/u = 1/30 and u = 30 cm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a 0.01 M HCl solution at 25 °C is:
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid: [H⁺] = 0.01 M, so pH = −log(10⁻²) = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.e: Electron-withdrawing halogens increase acidity through the −I effect; fluorine is the most electronegative, so FCH₂COOH is the strongest.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The site of photosynthesis in a plant cell is the:
questions.e: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplast, where chlorophyll captures light energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a C4 plant?
questions.e: Maize is a C4 plant (Kranz anatomy); wheat, rice and barley are C3 plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: The nephron — glomerulus plus tubule — is the structural and functional unit of the kidney.

questions.subject: Exam Info
questions.q: As of September 2026, the NTA 2026–27 examination calendar with respect to NEET UG 2027:
o: lists the exam on 2 May 2027 in CBT mode
does not list NEET UG 2027 dates; they will be announced separately
lists the exam on 2 May 2027 in pen-and-paper mode
questions.e: The released NTA 2026–27 calendar omits NEET UG 2027 (along with CUET UG 2027 and JEE Main Session 2) — dates will follow in a separate announcement. 2 May 2027 remains only a tentative expectation.

questions.subject: Exam Info
questions.q: The Centre has announced that NEET will move to which mode from next year?
questions.e: Following the paper-leak controversy, the Centre announced NEET will be conducted as a Computer Based Test from next year; the Radhakrishnan Committee had recommended phased CBT or hybrid modes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of resistance 12 Ω is bent into a circle. The resistance between two points at the ends of a diameter is:
questions.e: The two semicircles (6 Ω each) are in parallel: (6 × 6)/(6 + 6) = 3 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm forms an image twice as large as the object. The possible object distances are:
questions.e: |v/u| = 2. Real image: v = 2u ⇒ 1/20 = 1/2u + 1/u ⇒ u = 30 cm; virtual image: v = −2u ⇒ u = 10 cm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The half-life of a first-order reaction is 30 minutes. The time required for 75% completion is:
questions.e: 75% completion means two half-lives have passed (50% then 25% remaining): 2 × 30 = 60 minutes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.e: Sucrose has no free aldehyde or ketone group (the glycosidic bond links both anomeric carbons), so it cannot reduce Fehling's or Tollen's reagents.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The primary CO₂ acceptor in C3 plants is:
questions.e: In the Calvin cycle, RuBP (a 5-carbon compound) accepts CO₂ under the action of RuBisCO to form two molecules of 3-PGA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The hormone primarily responsible for apical dominance is:
questions.e: Auxin produced in the shoot apex suppresses lateral bud growth (apical dominance); cytokinins counteract it.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The SA node is located in the:
questions.e: The sinoatrial (SA) node, the heart's natural pacemaker, lies in the wall of the right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Army Dental Corps SSC Officer Recruitment 2026 (37 posts) requires candidates to have appeared in:
questions.e: Only candidates who appeared in NEET (MDS)-2026 (held 2 May 2026) are eligible; applications run 22 September-22 October 2026 on join.afms.gov.in.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: World Heart Day (29 September) uses the campaign 'Don't Miss a Beat'. The human heart is best described as a:
questions.e: The human heart is a double pump: the right side drives pulmonary circulation and the left side drives systemic circulation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula of pressure is:
questions.e: Pressure = force/area; [F] = [MLT^-2], [A] = [L^2], so [P] = [ML^-1T^-2].

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During photosynthesis, the oxygen released comes from:
questions.e: Photolysis of water in PS-II releases O2; shown by the classic experiments with isotopic oxygen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Human blood pH is maintained around:
questions.e: Blood pH is buffered at about 7.4 (slightly alkaline) by the bicarbonate buffer system.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: EOS-05, launched 4 September 2026, is India's first imaging satellite designed for geosynchronous orbit. A geostationary orbit has a period of:
questions.e: A geostationary orbit matches Earth's rotation period - 24 hours - so the satellite appears fixed over the equator.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of 0.01 M HCl is 2 because:
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid; [H+] = 0.01 M gives pH = -log(10^-2) = 2.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Channelrhodopsin, central to the 2026 Nobel-winning optogenetics work, was first identified in:
questions.e: Peter Hegemann's work began with how Chlamydomonas moves towards light; announced 5 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries concerning:
questions.e: Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel — optogenetics; prize money 12 million Swedish kronor.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Great Indian Bustard, two of which were released into Desert National Park in October 2026, is classified as:
questions.e: Released during National Wildlife Week (2–8 Oct, 72nd edition).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: India's cheetah population reached 60 in October 2026 with:
questions.e: Reported 6 Oct 2026 in current-affairs compilations.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The theme of National Wildlife Week 2026 is:
questions.e: 72nd edition, observed 2–8 October 2026.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: eSanjeevani, which crossed 50 crore online consultations, is India's:
questions.e: Run by the Health Ministry; milestone reported for 15 September 2026.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In autocatalysis — the phenomenon in Kagan and Soai's 2026 Chemistry Nobel — the catalyst is:
o: A product of the reaction itself
questions.e: Non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The NEET PG 2026 answer key was released by:
questions.e: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences released it in early October 2026.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to:
o: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel
questions.e: For optogenetics — controlling nerve cells with light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Optogenetics works by expressing light-sensitive proteins called:
questions.e: Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsins in algae; Deisseroth applied them to control neurons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In optogenetics, blue light typically ___ neurons expressing channelrhodopsin-2:
questions.e: Channelrhodopsin-2 is a light-gated cation channel; opening it lets positive ions in.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The IceCube Neutrino Observatory, cited in the 2026 Physics Nobel, is located at/in:
o: the South Pole, buried in Antarctic ice
questions.e: Francis Halzen won for decisive contributions to IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Neutrinos are hard to detect because they:
o: have no electric charge and interact only weakly
questions.e: Billions pass through the human body every second unnoticed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Navi Pillay, the 2026 Peace laureate, chaired a UN commission of inquiry on:
questions.e: She also served as a judge of the International Criminal Court and the Rwanda tribunal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organelle converts light energy to chemical energy, the natural counterpart of optogenetic light-sensing?
questions.e: Chlorophyll in thylakoids captures photons for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Francis Halzen is affiliated with:
questions.e: The Belgian-American particle physicist is 82.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: Cervavac, which received WHO prequalification in October 2026, is:
questions.e: Developed by the Serum Institute of India; WHO prequalification effective 25 Sept 2026.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: Cervavac is a quadrivalent vaccine targeting HPV types:
questions.e: Types 16 and 18 are high-risk strains linked to several cancers.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: Cervavac is indicated for:
questions.e: Two doses for 9–14 years (6 months apart); three doses for 15–26 years.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: WHO prequalification of Cervavac means it:
o: Can be procured by UN agencies
questions.e: It is SII's 32nd WHO prequalification for products/biologicals.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: The ongoing DRC Ebola outbreak is caused by the:
questions.e: No approved vaccine or specific treatment exists for the Bundibugyo strain.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: As of 6 Oct 2026, the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak recorded:
questions.e: The largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the DRC.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: The ChAdOx1 BDBV candidate vaccine, whose Phase Ib trials began in Uganda on 6 Oct 2026, was developed by:
questions.e: Announced by the Africa CDC; a Moderna candidate got ethical approval on 7 Oct.

questions.subject: Biology / Health
questions.q: HPV types 6 and 11 are commonly associated with:
questions.e: Types 16 and 18 are the high-risk cancer-linked strains Cervavac also covers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The 2026 Chemistry Nobel (Kagan/Soai) explains 'homochirality', which means:
o: Living organisms use only one mirror-image form of molecules like amino acids
All molecules in nature are symmetric
questions.e: From the Greek 'cheir' (hand); mirror-image molecules are 'chiral'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other are called:
questions.e: They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A 50:50 mixture of two enantiomers is called a:
questions.e: It is optically inactive because the rotations cancel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Enantiomers differ from each other in:
questions.e: All scalar physical properties are identical; only interaction with polarised light and chiral environments differs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The thalidomide tragedy is the classic example of:
o: One enantiomer being therapeutic while the other is teratogenic
questions.e: It drives the modern demand for single-enantiomer drugs — the field Kagan and Soai advanced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One variant of limonene smells of orange and the other of lemon because they are:
questions.e: Cited in the 2026 Chemistry Nobel coverage — mirror images can smell different.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Soai's contribution to the 2026 Chemistry Nobel was demonstrating:
o: Asymmetric autocatalysis — a chiral product catalysing its own formation
questions.e: The Soai reaction amplifies a tiny initial imbalance into a single dominant mirror image.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Amino acids in proteins are almost exclusively:
questions.e: The homochirality of life — the puzzle the 2026 Chemistry Nobel illuminated.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The scientific name of the cheetah is:
questions.e: Project Cheetah's reintroduction target; cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952 and are being reintroduced from Namibia and South Africa since 2022.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in the year:
questions.e: Project Cheetah began in September 2022 with eight cheetahs from Namibia; 40 of India's 59 cheetahs (as of 12 Oct 2026) were born in India.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In C4 plants, the first stable product of CO2 fixation (Hatch–Slack cycle) is:
questions.e: A 4-carbon compound formed in mesophyll cells; phosphoglyceric acid is the first product of the C3 Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria is best supported by the fact that they possess:
o: their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes
questions.e: Mitochondrial DNA is circular like bacterial DNA, and their 70S ribosomes match prokaryotic ribosomes — evidence for descent from engulfed bacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Who received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine?
o: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel
questions.e: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, announced on 5 October 2026, went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: For which discovery was the 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine awarded?
questions.e: The 2026 Medicine Nobel recognised optogenetics — a technique combining light and genetics to switch neurons on and off in living brains, built on the discovery of light-gated ion channels (channelrhodopsins).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: What is the core principle of optogenetics?
o: Controlling neurons with light via light-sensitive channels
questions.e: Optogenetics uses light-sensitive ion channels (e.g., channelrhodopsin) expressed in neurons so that pulses of light can activate or silence specific neurons — letting researchers map brain circuits. It merges optics with genetic targeting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Channelrhodopsins, central to the 2026 Nobel-winning work, are best described as:
questions.e: Channelrhodopsins are light-gated ion channels: when illuminated, they open and let ions (e.g., Na⁺, Ca²⁺) flow across the membrane, changing the neuron’s membrane potential and triggering or blocking firing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Aboard SpaceX CRS-35 (launched 13 Oct 2026), a precision-health investigation studies how antibiotic-resistant bacteria survive in microgravity. This is its:
o: Fourth and final planned stay aboard the ISS
questions.e: The investigation returns for its fourth and final planned stay aboard the ISS, sampling station surfaces for drug-resistant organisms — work relevant to both astronaut health and understanding superbugs on Earth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The International Big Cat Alliance, headquartered in New Delhi from 12 October 2026, works on seven species. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.e: IBCA covers tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma — a treaty-based intergovernmental effort inaugurated at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, on 12 October 2026.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of these is among the health research delivered to the ISS by SpaceX CRS-35 on 13 October 2026?
questions.e: CRS-35 delivered research into vision restoration, heart tissue, brain disorders and advanced materials, alongside the final pair of ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was shared by Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for work on:
questions.e: The trio was honoured for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels, the basis of optogenetics — controlling nerve cells with light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Channelrhodopsin, central to optogenetics, is a:
questions.e: Channelrhodopsin is a light-gated ion channel: it opens in response to light, allowing ions to flow and switching the neuron on or off.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for:
o: Non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell' because it generates most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration?
questions.e: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration — the Krebs cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix and oxidative phosphorylation along the inner membrane — producing most of the cell's ATP; hence 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The double-helix model of DNA was proposed by Watson and Crick in which year?
questions.e: The double-helical model of DNA was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953 (building on X-ray diffraction data, including Rosalind Franklin's), published in Nature; it earned the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Insulin is secreted by which cells of the pancreas?
questions.e: Insulin, which lowers blood glucose, is secreted by the beta (β) cells of the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas; alpha cells secrete glucagon.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The normal number of chromosomes in a human somatic cell is:
questions.e: The human somatic cell carries 46 chromosomes (23 pairs: 22 autosome pairs plus one pair of sex chromosomes).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The Krebs (citric acid) cycle takes place in the:
questions.e: The Krebs (citric acid) cycle enzymes are located in the mitochondrial matrix, while the electron transport chain operates along the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which blood group is regarded as the universal donor for red blood cell transfusion?
questions.e: Group O negative red cells carry neither A nor B antigens and the plasma carries no Rh factor issues for the recipient, making O-negative the universal red-cell donor (while AB-positive is the universal recipient).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During the Krebs cycle, the acetyl group of acetyl-CoA (2 carbons) is completely oxidised. How many molecules of CO2, NADH and FADH2 are produced per acetyl-CoA in one turn of the cycle?
questions.e: One turn of the Krebs cycle yields 2 CO2, 3 NADH, 1 FADH2 and 1 GTP (via substrate-level phosphorylation) per acetyl-CoA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a dihybrid cross (AaBb × AaBb), what proportion of the offspring are expected to show the dominant phenotype for both traits?
questions.e: The classic dihybrid phenotypic ratio is 9:3:3:1; the dominant–dominant class is 9/16.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pacemaker of the human heart, which initiates the cardiac impulse, is the:
questions.e: The sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium is the primary pacemaker, generating rhythmic impulses at ~70–75 per minute.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), ΔH = −92 kJ/mol, increasing the pressure at constant temperature will:
questions.e: The forward reaction converts 4 moles of gas to 2; by Le Chatelier's principle, increased pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (fewer gas moles). Kc depends only on temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm forms a real, inverted image of the same size as the object. The object distance from the lens is:
questions.e: A same-size real image forms when the object is at 2F; with F = 20 cm, the object distance is 40 cm and the image forms at 2F on the other side.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.e: Water is absorbed mainly by root hairs (increasing surface area) and transported upward through the xylem vessels driven by transpiration pull.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.e: Glucose is a monomer (a monosaccharide), whereas starch, cellulose and proteins are polymers built from repeated units.

questions.e: At 25°C, pure water has [H+] = 10⁻⁷ mol/L, so pH = −log(10⁻⁷) = 7.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.e: At 25°C, neutral solutions have [H+] = 10−7 M, so pH = 7.

questions.e: Electric current is measured in amperes (A) — one of the seven SI base units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Centaurus X-3, studied by RRI scientists in October 2026, is an example of a:
questions.e: Centaurus X-3 is a high-mass X-ray binary: a highly magnetised neutron star (pulsar) + a companion star of >10 solar masses, ~24,000 light years away. RRI (Oct 2026) found it accretes via an accretion disk — rare for its class. Extreme gravity pulls the companion's matter in, emitting X-rays.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Matter spiralling through an accretion disk around a neutron star radiates most strongly in which band?
questions.e: An accretion disk forms when matter spirals into a compact object, heating by friction/viscosity and radiating — in X-ray binaries, as X-rays. Finding one around Centaurus X-3 (a pulsar) is rare because pulsars' strong magnetic fields usually channel matter onto the magnetic poles instead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes, the main source of genetic variation, occurs in:
questions.e: During prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis) and exchange segments — crossing over — producing new allele combinations. This is the chief source of genetic variation in sexually reproducing organisms (along with independent assortment in metaphase I).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organelle produces most of the cell's ATP through oxidative phosphorylation?
questions.e: The mitochondrion generates ATP by oxidative phosphorylation: the electron transport chain pumps protons across the inner membrane, and ATP synthase uses the gradient to make ATP. Hence “powerhouse of the cell.” Muscle cells are mitochondrion-rich.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The synthesis of RNA from a DNA template is called:
questions.e: DNA → RNA is transcription (in the nucleus); RNA → protein is translation (at ribosomes). The central dogma: DNA → RNA → protein. Reverse transcription (RNA → DNA) occurs in retroviruses via reverse transcriptase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.e: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the ohm (Ω); siemens is conductance, farad is capacitance and henry is inductance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.e: The nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney; the glomerulus is only the filtration tuft within it.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): The SA node is called the pacemaker of the heart.
Reason (R): The SA node has the highest rate of spontaneous depolarisation among the nodal tissues, so it sets the rhythm of the heartbeat.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: SAN (sino-atrial node) generates impulses at the fastest rate (~70–75/min) and initiates each heartbeat — that is exactly why it is the pacemaker.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Insulin lowers blood glucose level.
Reason (R): Insulin stimulates cellular glucose uptake and glycogenesis, while inhibiting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: Insulin (β-cells of islets of Langerhans) acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, accelerating glucose uptake, storage as glycogen, and blocking glucose production — hence blood glucose falls.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Vascular bundles in a dicot stem are described as conjoint, collateral and open.
Reason (R): In dicot stems, cambium is present between the xylem and phloem of each bundle.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: “Open” specifically means cambium (fascicular cambium) is present between xylem and phloem, permitting secondary growth. Conjoint = xylem and phloem together; collateral = phloem outside, xylem inside on the same radius.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Crossing over takes place during the pachytene stage of prophase I.
Reason (R): Chiasmata become visible during the diplotene stage.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: Both statements are NCERT-true — crossing over (enzyme recombinase) occurs at pachytene and chiasmata are seen at diplotene — but the visibility of chiasmata does not explain why crossing over occurs at pachytene.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Bt cotton is resistant to bollworm infestation.
Reason (R): Activated cry toxins create pores in the insect’s gut cells, causing swelling, lysis and death.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: cryIAc and cryIIAb proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis are produced as inactive protoxins; the insect gut’s alkaline pH activates them, and the pores they form kill the gut cells — this is the mechanism of resistance.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction.
Reason (R): In this disorder, autoantibodies block and destroy acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: NCERT lists myasthenia gravis as an auto-immune disorder of the neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscles — caused by anti-receptor antibodies.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Photorespiration is negligible in C4 plants.
Reason (R): In C4 plants, initial CO2 fixation by PEP carboxylase in mesophyll cells concentrates CO2 around RuBisCO in bundle-sheath cells.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: The CO₂-concentrating mechanism keeps the CO₂:O₂ ratio high at the RuBisCO site, suppressing its oxygenase activity — so photorespiration is effectively absent in C4 plants.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Testosterone is a steroid hormone.
Reason (R): Testosterone is secreted by the Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testes.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: Both are true — testosterone is indeed a steroid secreted by Leydig cells — but the site of secretion does not explain its chemical nature (it is a steroid because it is derived from cholesterol).

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Curare causes flaccid paralysis of skeletal muscles.
Reason (R): Curare competitively blocks acetylcholine receptors on the motor end plate.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: By occupying ACh receptors without opening the ion channel, curare prevents depolarisation of the muscle fibre — the classic pharmacology behind neuromuscular-blocking drugs (and the exam’s favourite A–R pair on this topic).

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): In the lac operon, lactose acts as an inducer.
Reason (R): Lactose (via allolactose) binds the repressor protein and inactivates it, freeing the operator.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: The lac i gene’s repressor normally sits on the operator; the inducer binds and inactivates it, so RNA polymerase can transcribe the structural genes z, y, a.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): Haemophilia shows a criss-cross pattern of inheritance.
Reason (R): The gene for clotting factor VIII is located on the X chromosome, and the disorder is X-linked recessive.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: Because the gene sits on the X chromosome, the trait passes from an affected father to grandsons through carrier daughters — the criss-cross pattern typical of X-linked recessive disorders.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Assertion (A): In C3 plants, photorespiration increases on hot, bright, dry days.
Reason (R): RuBisCO can bind both CO2 and O2, and its oxygenase activity rises when the CO2:O2 ratio at the active site falls (stomata close, internal CO2 drops).
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.e: RuBisCO’s dual affinity is the whole story: when stomata close to save water, CO₂ inside the leaf falls and O₂ from photolysis accumulates, so oxygenation (photorespiration) increases.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Statement I: DNA replication in E. coli is semi-conservative, as shown by Meselson and Stahl using ¹⁵N labelling and CsCl density-gradient centrifugation.
Statement II: In eukaryotes, DNA replication takes place during the S phase of interphase.
o: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
questions.e: Both are standard NCERT facts: the Meselson–Stahl experiment proved semi-conservative replication, and eukaryotic DNA replicates in S phase.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Statement I: The Golgi apparatus is the primary site of protein synthesis in the cell.
Statement II: Lysosomes are rich in hydrolytic enzymes that work best at an acidic pH.
o: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
questions.e: Protein synthesis happens on ribosomes (the Golgi only modifies, packages and dispatches proteins). Lysosomal hydrolases are indeed acid-active — Statement II alone is correct.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Statement I: In human beings, the sex of the child is determined by the mother.
Statement II: Grasshoppers show the XO type of sex determination, where males have only one X chromosome.
o: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
questions.e: In humans the father determines sex (X- or Y-bearing sperm). The grasshopper XO system is a correct NCERT example of male heterogamety.

questions.subject: Assertion-Reason
questions.q:
Statement I: Vaccination works because the immune system retains a memory of the antigen it first encounters.
Statement II: Anti-tetanus serum gives passive immunity because it contains pre-formed antibodies.
o: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct: active immunity (vaccines) relies on immunological memory, while ready-made antibodies (ATS, anti-venom Ig) give immediate passive immunity.

o: only in pen-and-paper mode as before
in hybrid mode with no written paper
